entries.abstract: Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) underwent major fragmentation after its 2025 October 8 perihelion passage at q ~ 0.33 au. We present four epochs of Johnson-Cousins BVR imaging obtained with the Mount Laguna Observatory 40-inch reflector on 2025 November 26, November 29, December 5, and December 8, sampling the subsequent evolution of the integrated fragment-coma complex. The images were homogenized to common circular two-dimensional effective point-spread functions before morphology was measured along the projected fragment axis. We evaluated 324 profile-extraction configurations and removed solutions whose localized peak landed on the search-window boundary. The fragment-axis surface-brightness enhancement relocates inward between November 26 and 29 and outward between December 5 and 8; the sign of both changes is recovered in every valid configuration and at all tested common target PSFs from 5.3 to 6.0 arcsec. Calibrated BVR photometry using Gaia DR3 synthetic Johnson-Kron-Cousins standards independently shows a repeatable November 26-29 change in broadband spectral shape: B-V decreases while V-R increases. The curvature index S'_(V-R) - S'_(B-V) changes by +3.47 (+1.50/-1.65) percent per 1000 Angstrom, with 99.1 percent of Monte Carlo realizations positive, while the full B-R reflectivity gradient remains approximately constant. Repeating the color comparison at a fixed projected radius of 2205 km produces nearly identical changes. The combined results are consistent with continued restructuring of the unresolved post-fragmentation inner coma, while broadband imaging alone cannot uniquely separate dust-color evolution, molecular emission, and changing contributions from unresolved fragments.

entries.title: EP241021a as An Off-nuclear Month-duration Transient in a Dwarf Starburst Galaxy
entries.abstract: EP241021a is a peculiar fast X-ray transient exhibiting a long X-ray plateau and an optical rebrightening, both challenging the traditional jet afterglow model. Whether its nature is a stellar explosion or a tidal disruption event (TDE) remains debated. Here we present late-time HST/WFC3 and Gemini-N/GMOS observations of its host galaxy at $z=0.748$. After $\sim300$ days post-trigger, the transient emission had faded below detection, revealing a dwarf disk galaxy with an effective radius $R_e=1.7$ kpc, a stellar mass $M_\star\sim3\times10^8M_\odot$, and a high star formation rate of $\sim5\ M_\odot\ {\rm yr}^{-1}$. Combined with previous very long baseline interferometry measurements, the transient can be located in the galactic disk with a projected physical offset of $0.95\pm0.13$ kpc from the galaxy center. Host-subtracted optical light curves show that the rebrightening ceased at $\sim47$ days, followed by a sudden drop with a power-law index steeper than $-3.3$, coincident with a similar drop in the X-ray light curve. This synchronous drop in both bands is consistent with jet shut-off, and the required month-long jet activity suggests a persistently accreting compact object fed by a TDE. Among the TDE scenarios, the off-nuclear location and the starburst host galaxy slightly favor the post-supernova micro-TDE scenario in a binary system, in which a natal kick drives the newborn compact object into a tidal disruption of its companion. Nevertheless, an off-nuclear intermediate-mass black hole TDE or a stellar-mass black hole TDE induced by dynamical scattering in a dense stellar cluster cannot yet be excluded.

entries.title: Survey of small amplitude waves in solar prominences
entries.abstract: Presence of small amplitude oscillation or waves in solar prominences was investigated by using archived data from a full disk H-alpha imaging spectroscopic observation. A total of 178 prominences on the limb were studied and it was found that there are plenty of evidence of oscillations or waves with preferential periods in 3 - 5 min (4 min) and 10 - 20 min (15 min). We found very clear signature of persistently propagating 4 min wave in 21 prominences and at least a hint of 4 min oscillation in 90 prominences in their Doppler signal. The 4 min waves are often found in prominences with a large horizontal size, and they propagate in nearly horizontal direction with a phase speed of 140 - 400 km/s. On the other hand, very clear evidence of the 15 min wave was found in 14 prominences and at least a hint of oscillation in 62 prominences in the Doppler signal. The 15 min waves preferentially propagate in vertical direction with a phase speed of 20 - 50 km/s. There is a positive correlation between the presences of 4 min and 15 min waves. The 4 min waves are interpreted as Alfvenic wave propagating along the coronal magnetic field supporting the prominences. Two scenarios are discussed for the 15 min wave, i.e., Alfvenic wave propagating vertically in prominence bodies and apparent cross-field propagation in magnetic structures. Prominences that harbor the short period waves or oscillations distribute over the entire solar latitude, suggesting that these waves are excited by ubiquitous disturbance in solar atmosphere. While it is also true that a number of prominences do not show signatures of oscillations nor propagating waves, and the reason of this diversity remains open question. Our study suggests that observing the 4 min waves in prominences will serve as a useful tool for tracing the coronal Alfvenic waves and the magnetic field supporting the prominences.

entries.title: Probing In-Medium Neutron-to-Dark-Fermion Conversion with Multimessenger Neutron Star Observations
entries.abstract: Neutron stars provide a natural environment for probing in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion and its impact on the dense-matter equation of state (EOS). We use multimessenger neutron star observations to map excluded and not-excluded regions of dark-sector parameter space for an EOS ensemble within a non-linear $σ$--$ω$--$ρ$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework and determine their overlap across the ensemble. We include a fermionic dark component with repulsive self-interactions of strength $G_χ$. We consider masses $m_χ$ near the neutron mass and heavier states accessible in neutron star cores at sufficiently large neutron chemical potentials. To reduce sensitivity to the nucleonic EOS within this framework, we scan $m_χ=939$--$1500$ MeV and $G_χ=1$--$100$ fm$^2$ across 21 nucleonic EOSs: a main baseline set of 13 EOSs and soft and stiff limiting cases. Stellar sequences are tested against the requirement that the EOS support at least $2M_\odot$ neutron stars, GW170817 tidal-deformability bounds, and NICER mass--radius constraints, considering the Illinois--Maryland and X-PSI/Amsterdam inference sets separately. For the full ensemble of 21 EOSs, both NICER analyses identify similar regions excluded by all EOSs, with approximate minimum--maximum extents of $m_χ=939$--$1300$ MeV and $G_χ=1$--$11$ fm$^2$. Unlike the full 21-EOS ensemble, the main baseline set has a common not-excluded region whose extent depends on the NICER analysis. The soft and stiff limiting cases show how these regions shift when the nucleonic EOS predicts a maximum neutron star mass near $2M_\odot$ or large tidal deformabilities. Across these 21 calibrated nucleonic RMF EOSs, weak dark-sector repulsion is robustly disfavored across a broad dark-fermion mass range, while the extent of the remaining not-excluded region depends on the NICER analysis and baryonic EOS stiffness.

entries.title: Contributions of massive stars and classical novae to Galactic 26Al
entries.abstract: The radioactive isotope 26Al is believed to be mainly produced by massive stars and ejected into the interstellar medium through their winds and supernovae. Due to its lifetime of 1.04 Myr, it traces recent nucleosynthesis and star formation. 60Fe is a similarly long-lived (lifetime 3.8 Myr) isotope, and only originating in ccSNe. Stellar evolution models in combination with Galactic Chemical Evolution (GCE) models tend to over-predict the 60Fe/26Al ratio. Population synthesis models that attempt to explain both, the 26Al mass in the Galaxy and its spatial distribution, only match the observational constraints with an enhanced star formation rate (SFR) of >5 Msun/yr. Classical novae may contribute to the 26Al production, potentially lowering the SFR inferred from massive stars and alleviating tension in the 60Fe/26Al ratio. However, previous studies suggest their contribution is negligible or < 10%. In this work we aim to determine the mass distribution of 26Al as a function of Galactocentric radius and estimate the contribution of (very) massive stars and classical novae to the 1.8 MeV signal. We are using 20 yr of INTEGRAL/SPI observations of the gamma-ray line at 1.8 MeV to test different assumptions on the radial structure of 26Al and compare the resulting mass distribution to different GCE models. For our baseline analysis, all tested source models prefer substantial nova contributions, with best-fit fractions of 77-84%. This alleviates tension in the 60Fe/26Al ratio and lowers the SFR from 26Al measurements accordingly to 1-2 Msun/yr. While it is difficult to gauge both contributions directly, next generation MeV telescopes can potentially identify individual massive stars, such as Gamma-2-Velorum.

entries.title: The origin and distribution of diffuse HI in the close interacting MHONGOOSE galaxy systems
entries.abstract: We present the deepest HI observations of the two systems with Dproj < 100 kpc, and $Δ$ vsys < 200 km/s in the MHONGOOSE survey. The MeerKAT observations have a 3$σ$ NHI = 10$^{17.9}$ cm$^{-2}$ over 16 km/s at 4 kpc scales. The new data detect HI in seven galaxies -- the interacting NGC 3511/3513 pair, and an interacting triplet (NGC 4781, NGC 4790 and UGCA 308) along with two new (2MASX J1255 and MKT 25413) dwarf satellites. Six galaxies lie on the star-forming main sequence, and their HI gas fractions are typical for such systems. In contrast, MKT 25413 has a log(MHI/Msun) = 5.7, which is the lowest MHI detected of a galaxy that is not a Milky Way satellite. This low surface brightness dwarf galaxy shows an anomalously low star formation and HI fraction for its stellar mass. We find ubiquitous low column density HI surrounding the galaxies, which is likely a consequence of mild tidal interactions from fly-bys in the past few hundred megayears. We derive the stellar and H$α$ kinematics from VLT/MUSE observations and the H2 kinematics from ALMA observations. The kinematics of the stellar and multiphase interstellar medium of the interacting galaxies display ordered rotation, and the atomic-to-molecular gas ratios are indistinguishable from star-forming field galaxies. The stellar morphology of all the interacting galaxies (except the low-mass dwarf UGCA 308) does not show major disruptions, and there is no stellar component associated with the HI tails, bridges or clouds in the intra-group mediums, down to $μ_{g}$ = 29 mag arcsec$^{-2}$. We surmise that the mild environmental interactions in the close systems are able to pull the diffuse HI out of the disk and redistribute it. The gas is not in equilibrium, although it remains bound and is in the process of falling back onto the disk.

entries.title: ePNGCAT: the first eROSITA all-sky data release
entries.abstract: The eROSITA telescope array aboard the joint German--Russian Spektrum-Roentgen-Gamma (SRG) mission delivered the deepest soft all-sky X-ray survey to date, scanning the entire sky more than four times between December 2019 and February 2022. The potential of the survey remains, however, hampered by the fact that only data for the half of the sky owned by the German consortium have been released publicly, whereas the other half remains accessible only to the Russian consortium, effectively making eROSITA a "half-sky" survey for most applications. The only publicly accessible all-sky "data product" as of 2026 is a single press-release image published in June 2020 jointly by both consortia to celebrate the completion of the first all-sky survey (eRASS1). Here I present the first all-sky eROSITA catalogue based on this image, containing around 63 thousand sources with an estimated completeness of about 50% above $3\times10^{-13}$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ in the 0.2-2.3 keV band and a positional accuracy of $\sim$1 arcmin, validated against the full eRASS1 catalogue for half the sky and against several external catalogues. The catalogue is thus comparable with 2RXS, the deepest truly all-sky survey generally available, and gives a first glimpse of the eastern Galactic hemisphere with eROSITA. In this hemisphere, about 11000 detected sources have no counterpart in ROSAT or other public X-ray catalogues and are expected to be genuine new X-ray sources. Besides the catalogue, I release calibrated HEALPix maps to facilitate studies of large-scale extended emission, such as the eROSITA bubbles, or of Galactic absorption that require full sky coverage (https://zenodo.org/records/23640281), as well as the complete analysis pipeline to make the results fully reproducible (https://github.com/doroshv/eropngcat).

entries.title: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
entries.abstract: This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. Particular emphasis is placed on observables that connect finite-nucleus structure to bulk properties of nuclear matter, including neutron-skin thicknesses, electric dipole polarizabilities, and monopole sum rules. We discuss how neutron skins and dipole polarizabilities provide information on the density dependence of the symmetry energy, while monopole observables constrain the incompressibility of nuclear matter.

entries.title: Theoretical Pulsation Properties of RR Lyrae and Type II Cepheids in the JWST and Roman photometric systems
entries.abstract: RR Lyrae (RRL) stars and Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are key standard candles and tracers of old stellar populations. The deep, wide-field capabilities of facilities such as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will significantly expand their utility as a Population II alternative to Classical Cepheids for distance scale calibrations. We present theoretical pulsation properties-including light-curve morphologies, amplitudes, and multi-filter relations for RRLs (Z = 0.0001 - 0.02, M = 0.51 - 0.80, Msun) and T2Cs (Z = 0.0001 - 0.01, M = 0.495 - 0.65, Msun) to enable detailed studies of Galactic and extragalactic populations. Using alreday available non-linear convective pulsation models, we converted their predicted bolometric light curves across various chemical compositions and evolutionary stages into the JWST and Roman photometric systems. From these, we derived multi-filter Period-Amplitude and Color-Color diagrams, alongside Period-Luminosity and Period-Wesenheit relations with explicit metallicity terms. RRL relations display a significantly stronger zero-point metallicity dependence than those of T2Cs, despite sharing similar slopes. Consequently, T2Cs offer a distance scale indicator that is remarkably robust against metallicity uncertainties. As a preliminary test, we applied our metal-dependent Period-Wesenheit relations to a subset of JWST-observed RRLs in the WLM galaxy, deriving a distance modulus of mu_0 = 24.85 +/- 0.03 mag (assuming the literature average metallicity). The derived distance to WLM is consistent with most literature values, though slightly shorter than determinations based on Classical Cepheids and the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. These theoretical relations pave the way for future high-precision distance determinations and asteroseismic diagnostics with JWST and Roman.

entries.title: Resolving a Clumpy Disk Wind in 4U 1957+115 with XRISM
entries.abstract: We present a high-resolution XRISM/Resolve observation of the persistent black hole candidate 4U 1957+115, revealing the first detection of an intrinsic disk wind in this source. The absorption is dominated by highly ionized Fe XXV and Fe XXVI and varies substantially throughout the observation, becoming prominent during the final $\sim40$ ks despite a modest decrease of only $\sim5$--$10\%$ in source flux. The observed evolution of the absorption cannot be explained solely by ionization changes driven by the modest continuum variability, favoring an inhomogeneous outflow with evolving line-of-sight properties. Time-resolved spectroscopy reveals substantially narrower absorption features in shorter intervals, with the inferred turbulent velocity decreasing from $\sim350~{\rm km/s}$ in the longer integration to $\lesssim70~{\rm km/s}$ in the shortest selections. This suggests that the broader absorption profiles measured over longer integrations may result, at least in part, from averaging over an evolving wind rather than from intrinsically larger turbulent velocities. Such time averaging can therefore affect the inferred physical properties of the wind and complicate efforts to identify its launching mechanism. Even though the wind carries only a small fraction of the radiative luminosity in kinetic form, its mass-loss rate may remain dynamically relevant. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved, high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy for characterizing the structure and variability of accretion disk winds.

entries.title: Data-driven segmentation of solar filaments based on ground-based instrument data
entries.abstract: The dynamic behavior of solar prominences and filaments is a precursor to coronal mass ejections (CMEs), which can disrupt Earth's magnetosphere and affect satellite communications. Systematic ground-based solar observations, conducted with high temporal resolution, are instrumental in monitoring these structures. Analysis of the morphological changes and destabilization processes of filaments and prominences captured in datasets can help identify early warning signs of potential eruptions. This capability is vital for developing reliable space weather forecasting systems, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of solar disturbances on Earth's technological infrastructure. Previously, we introduced hybrid algorithmic-data driven method which performance was shown on a set of Solar Dynamic Observatory (SDO) Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) instrument data performing segmentation of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and shock waves. In this work, we extend certain aspects of this approach to image segmentation of solar features -- filaments and prominences using H-alpha Kanzelhohe Observatory data. We describe a leakage-aware, sparse multi-year sampling strategy. We present image segmentation models pre-trained on synoptic and normalized image data, followed by a discussion of how model performance depends on training-set engineering, data preprocessing techniques, and the choice of loss metrics. We perform a limited study, both analytically and numerically, of the effect of external, fixed normalization versus native input for compact U-Net-based segmentation of solar H-alpha filaments, also contributing to ongoing research on normalization in deep networks in general and compact models in particular.

entries.title: Magnetic Topological Evolution and the Predictive Role of Winding-flux-based Masked PILs in Extreme Solar Flares from AR13664 and AR13842
entries.abstract: Using vector magnetogram data from the Helioseismic Magnetic Imager (HMI) on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present detailed case studies of precursor activity in Active Regions (ARs) 13664 and 13842, which produced several intense flares. We examined the spatiotemporal evolution of key magnetic topological parameters, including winding, helicity, winding-flux-based masked polarity inversion lines (PILs), and PIL gradients, from the precursor to the post-flare phases. The temporal evolution of the winding flux showed a significant enhancement during the precursor phase, and this trend was consistent across the seven X-class and five M-class flares (>= M5.0). The spatial distribution of both raw and Gaussian-smoothed winding-flux enhancement is co-located with flare footpoint regions of highly twisted core fields, as indicated by the photospheric magnetic topology. The winding-flux-based masked PILs that persisted around the flare locations showed a significant increase in strength and area during the precursor activity. These masked PILs spatially coincide with regions likely hosting non-potential core magnetic fields associated with the observed flares. Furthermore, the gradient of strong PILs extracted from the ARs was positively correlated with flare-associated locations and typically increased several hours (approx. 3-5 h) before flare onset. By imposing a gradient threshold on strong PILs, we isolate magnetic regions repeatedly associated with flare initiation, providing useful constraints in regimes where current flare-forecasting models remain uncertain. Therefore, the combined analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of different magnetic topological parameters enhances our understanding of intense solar flare forecasting and the identification of potential triggering sites, thereby contributing to improved space weather prediction frameworks.

entries.title: Analytical modeling of the gamma-ray morphology of TeV halos around moving pulsars
entries.abstract: We aim to derive an analytical prescription for the line-of-sight-integrated particle distribution around moving pulsars, suitable for constructing spatial templates of the associated TeV-halo gamma-ray emission without resorting to computationally expensive numerical integrations. We consider electrons and positrons continuously injected by a moving source, undergoing isotropic diffusion and radiative energy losses. Assuming spatially uniform target photon fields, as appropriate for the cosmic microwave background and approximately valid for the interstellar radiation fields, the projected particle distribution provides a useful proxy for the inverse-Compton gamma-ray morphology. We show that the line-of-sight integration of the particle distribution can be performed exactly, reducing the calculation to a single numerical integral over the injection history. Under the additional assumptions of constant injection luminosity and a simplified treatment of energy losses, we derive a fully analytical expression that factorizes into an energy-dependent spectral term and a dimensionless spatial term describing the energy-dependent morphology. Comparison with the exact calculation shows good agreement over a broad range of energies and spatial scales, with appreciable deviations primarily at particle energies approaching the cutoff of the injection spectrum and at large distances from the source, where the emission becomes fainter. Our results enable the construction of physically motivated, energy-dependent spatial templates for gamma-ray halos around moving pulsars, capturing the morphological asymmetries induced by proper motion without computationally expensive numerical integrations. This makes them particularly suitable for systematic morphological and spectral analyses of extended gamma-ray sources.

entries.title: Magnetic switchback development from the evolution of torsional Alfvén waves
entries.abstract: Magnetic switchbacks are mostly Alfvénic local deflections, or even reversals, of the ambient magnetic field of the solar wind. Despite intense research their origin remains unclear and is highly debated. Here we describe a new simulation study demonstrating how torsional Alfvén waves can evolve into switchbacks. We use surface rotational motions to launch torsional Alfvén waves into the super-radially expanding magnetic field of a coronal hole. The simulations demonstrate that in such an expanding wind, the waves initially steepen as they propagate while also inducing a cylindrical parallel plasma jet. A combination of shear from the jet and wave evolution under the constraint of approximate spherical polarisation ($|\mathbf{B}|\approx const.$) then leads to the formation of switchbacks in a ring configuration. We explore the 3D nature of the switchbacks, how and where they from, and present scalings for their peak deflection and parallel and perpendicular length scales. We also derive an expression for switchback deflection in the linear regime which we contrast against our results. The results are discussed in relation to recent observations and previous switchback formation studies.

entries.title: Multiphase Gas Structure in JWST Little Red Dots
entries.abstract: JWST has uncovered a population of compact high-redshift galaxies, 'little red dots' (LRDs), exhibiting broad Balmer emission lines that often show narrow absorption features and strong Balmer breaks - spectral signatures attributed to dense gas surrounding rapidly growing black holes, but whose small-scale structure remains unknown. A striking feature of LRD spectra is that the H$β$ absorption is systematically deeper than H$α$, yet in any homogeneous gas this ordering is physically impossible. Here we model the H$α$ and H$β$ line profiles using radiative transfer simulations for 11 LRDs with JWST sensitive high resolution spectroscopy, and independently constrain the $n=2$ hydrogen column density, $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$, from the Balmer-break continuum. We find that the $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$ from H$α$ in a homogeneous medium cannot reproduce the observed H$β$ absorption in several objects, and that this $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$ typically falls two orders of magnitude below the lower bound set by the Balmer break. Both tensions are simultaneously resolved by a multiphase medium of dense clumps within diffuse hot ionized gas. This multiphase gas structure is a necessary ingredient for any viable LRD model, regardless of the nature of the central engine.

entries.title: Partial Fragmentation of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS)
entries.abstract: We present time-series observations of the long period comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) obtained in 2025-2026, bracketing the comet's fragmentation in early November 2025. We show that a simple radiation pressure model can explain many of the comet's properties: the rapid fading after fragmentation, the increasing mean particle size in the projected photometry aperture, and the time dependence of the surface brightness profile. Small dust particles ($\lesssim 100 μ$m) dominate the coma, with average dust velocity $\sim$ a few $\times$ 1 meter s$^{-1}$. The nucleus radius is estimated at $\sim$0.5 km and the dust properties are consistent with, but do not prove, an origin in nucleus rotational breakup, followed by being swept down the tail by radiation pressure.

entries.title: O VI Emission in Starbursting BCGs: An HST-COS Extension of "Reigniting the FUSE"
entries.abstract: In this extension of our "Reigniting the FUSE" series, we have obtained new far-ultraviolet spectroscopy of 3 starbursting brightest cluster galaxies with the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) aboard HST. With these new data, in combination with archival COS data of 2 additional systems, we measure star formation rates (SFRs) from the young stellar continuum and cooling rates through $10^{5.5}$ K gas with the O VI $1032,1038\,\mathring{\rm A}$ doublet ($\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI}$). We use these measurements to increase the size of the "Reigniting the FUSE" sample, which itself contains high resolution far UV spectroscopy for 29 nearby massive elliptical galaxies from FUSE, and extend it 1 dex upwards in SFR and cooling rate. Our derived SFRs agree well with photometric GALEX$+$WISE SFRs from the literature. The new data also reinforce the previously observed trend in cooling efficiency ($\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI}/\dot{M}_{\rm max}$; where $\dot{M}_{\rm max}$ is the X-ray luminosity-based cooling rate) versus mass, with groups cooling more efficiently than clusters by a factor of $\sim$4-5. When we isolate a sample of the most star-forming central galaxies, we find that the star formation rates, X-ray spectroscopic cooling rates, and UV spectroscopic cooling rates are all consistent with one another, on average, while retaining substantial system-to-system scatter, reflecting time-depenent multiphase condensation and cold gas reservoir evolution. The remainder of the sample, in contrast, overwhelmingly shows ratios of ${\rm SFR}/\dot{M}_{\rm O\,VI} \sim {\rm SFR}/\dot{M}_{\rm X,spec} \sim 10\%$.

entries.title: Reproducibility, Methodological Robustness, and Synthetic-Domain Selection Properties of AFINO for TESS Stellar-Flare QPP Analysis
entries.abstract: Quasi-periodic pulsation (QPP) searches in stellar flares depend on methodological choices that can affect both classification and the interpretation of recovered periods. A defensible assessment therefore requires explicit separation of reproducibility, robustness, and known-truth performance. We characterize the reproducibility, methodological robustness, numerical behavior, and synthetic-ground-truth selection properties of a frozen public AFINO implementation in the TESS context while keeping observational reference evidence separate from known synthetic truth. The frozen baseline reproduced five published TESS detections in the initial reproduction cohort. A ten-event observational pilot and a catalogue-scale robustness experiment then tested prospectively specified temporal-window and processing perturbations. At catalogue scale, 51 of 61 published-QPP references did not reproduce their frozen reference state under the F3A baseline, so robustness claims were conditioned on baseline-concordant references rather than interpreted as accuracy. In a separately developed synthetic programme, the untouched AFINO 0.5 rule was evaluated once on an independent HELDOUT set: 152 of 1800 synthetic positives were selected and no false selections were observed among 1800 synthetic nulls, with finite Wilson uncertainty. The resulting 156-stratum selection surface and period-recovery summaries remain conditional on the frozen synthetic domain and, for period recovery, on selection; they therefore provide a bounded characterization of methodological robustness and synthetic-domain selection behavior without establishing observational validation or a population-level correction.

entries.title: ODIN: Comparison of Source Extractor and Tractor Source Detection for Lyman Alpha Emitting Galaxy Selection at z=3.1
entries.abstract: Lyman Alpha Emitting galaxies (LAEs) are young, actively star-forming galaxies identified by their strong Lyman-alpha emission at a rest-frame wavelength of 121.6 nm, making them valuable tracers of galaxy evolution and the large-scale structure of the Universe. The One-hundred-deg^2 DECam Imaging in narrow-bands (ODIN) survey collects LAE samples during Cosmic Noon. Because LAE selection is based on photometric measurements derived from source-detection algorithms, the choice of detection method can directly affect the resulting LAE samples. We therefore compare two prominent source detection methods, Source Extractor (SE) and Tractor (Tr), to determine which is better suited for LAE selection in ODIN. We investigate differences between SE and Tr in the ODIN-COSMOS field, focusing on the z=3.1 LAE sample. We find that a significant fraction of Tr LAEs have low continuum flux measurements, increasing the inferred narrow-band excess and resulting in an LAE sample nearly twice as large as SE. However, LAEs detected by Tr but not SE exhibit equivalent width estimates indicative of potential contamination. We introduce an additional LAE selection criterion based on the expected Lyman-break behavior of LAEs at z~3 to reduce low-redshift contamination without requiring a significant detection of the break itself. Our results demonstrate that differences in source detection can significantly affect narrow-band LAE selection and motivate the use of SE photometry for ODIN LAE catalogs.

entries.title: Radio view of the Peanut cluster: merger-induced stripping and a radio halo shortly after pericentric passage
entries.abstract: The Peanut galaxy cluster (SRGe CL0238.3+2005) offers a rare opportunity to investigate thermal and nonthermal processes only $\sim0.1$\,Gyr after pericentric passage. We present a multi-frequency radio study of this system at $z=0.42$ using new MeerKAT and uGMRT observations, complemented by Chandra and MUSTANG-2 data. We identify two morphologically and spectrally distinct radio components: a double-lobed source in the northern subcluster and extended diffuse emission across the cluster center. The double-lobed source has a strongly curved, ultra-steep spectrum and is offset by $\sim22$\,kpc from the nearest brightest cluster galaxy. Its spectral curvature and positional offset are consistent with remnant AGN plasma that may have been displaced during the merger or reshaped by a shock. The diffuse emission extends over $\sim1$~Mpc and is classified as an ultra-steep spectrum ($α=-1.77\pm0.11$ between 400\,MHz and 1.28\,GHz) radio halo. Its volume-averaged radio emissivity, $(1.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-3}$ Hz$^{-1}$ at 1.4\,GHz, is an order of magnitude higher than the characteristic value for other halos. The radial profile of the halo is well described by a single exponential fit and its radio emission correlates tightly with the X-ray, with a best-fit slope of $1.11\pm0.05$. Chandra and MUSTANG-2 observations reveal candidate surface brightness discontinuities, with the most prominent inner feature coinciding with a region of flatter spectral index, potentially tracing localized particle (re)-acceleration. The coexistence of an extended ultra-steep spectrum radio halo, high radio emissivity, remnant AGN plasma, and candidate X-ray/SZ discontinuities makes the Peanut cluster an important test case for understanding the evolution of diffuse radio emission and its connection to the dynamical state of the intracluster medium in early-stage mergers.

entries.title: Machine Learning Applications in the Solar Interior and Atmosphere
entries.abstract: The solar interior and atmosphere constitute a strongly coupled, multiscale dynamical system defined by continuous temporal evolution. Predicting the state of this system requires modeling physical interactions that span disparate spatial and temporal scales, constrained by heterogeneous and sparse data. This chapter formalizes the Sun within the mathematical framework of dynamical systems theory, defining a global state vector ($\vec{S}$) governed by thermodynamical, kinetic, and magnetic properties. Because solar observations represent projected, multi-modal, and partially observable measurements ($\vec{O}[\vec{S}]$) of this hidden state, pure physics-based deduction is fundamentally constrained. We present a unifying thesis: the primary role of machine learning in heliophysics is to act as a structured family of mathematical operators---specifically Inference ($\mathcal{I}$), Emulation ($\mathcal{E}$), Propagation ($\mathcal{P}$), and Control ($\mathcal{C}$)---that reconstruct, simulate, and couple this global state vector across disparate physical layers. By framing the vast, multi-disciplinary literature within this unified state-space taxonomy, we demonstrate how data-driven techniques bridge observational gaps to resolve hidden multiscale couplings and dramatically accelerate the simulation of non-linear processes, establishing a rigorous pathway to predict the global evolution of the Sun.

entries.title: Binary Progenitors of Electron-capture Supernovae
entries.abstract: Electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) arise from a narrow progenitor parameter space between oxygen-neon white dwarf formation and iron-core collapse supernovae, governed by the competition between core growth and envelope removal. Binary interactions modify this balance through mass transfer and mergers. Using the binary population synthesis framework POSYDON, we model ECSN progenitors across metallicities from $Z/Z_\odot=2$ to $10^{-4}$, focusing on the initial parameter space, pre-supernova stripping, envelope-based classification, surviving companions, post-supernova orbits, and cosmic event rates. The lower edge of the binary ECSN initial primary mass lies near $7\,M_\odot$, owing to efficient convective overshooting in the POSYDON grids, whereas the upper edge increases with metallicity because stronger line-driven winds require larger initial masses to build carbon-oxygen cores within the ECSN range. Stable mass transfer and mergers occupy distinct regions in initial mass ratio and orbital period space. ECSNe in bound binaries are divided into hydrogen-rich Type II ($\sim30\%$), IIb ($\sim10\%$), and Ib ($\sim60\%$) outcomes according to residual hydrogen and helium envelopes. Across all channels, approximately one-third of ECSNe have a bound companion at explosion; the remaining two-thirds do not. Among these bound systems, approximately $90\%$ of the companions are main-sequence stars at explosion. These companions exhibit a bimodal spin distribution, including a rapidly rotating component associated with prior mass transfer. Evolved-star and compact-object companions each account for only a few percent. Combining the formation efficiencies with cosmic star formation and metallicity evolution models yields an intrinsic ECSN rate peaking at $z\sim2-3$ and declining at higher redshifts. Over cosmic history, ECSNe contribute approximately $1\%-4\%$ of all core-collapse supernovae.

entries.title: Gaia DR3 Compact Binary Candidates Constrained by Radial Velocity Measurements
entries.abstract: Astrometry enables the most direct determination of the orbital elements and component masses of compact binaries. The potential of the current Gaia data for this purpose has not yet been fully explored. In this work, we combine Gaia astrometric and radial velocity (RV) measurements to perform joint orbital fitting for 1,835 Gaia astrometric binaries with available RV data. Among the 518 systems with at least three effective RV epochs, we identify 171 compact binary candidates, including four with inferred dark companion masses exceeding 2.1 $M_{\odot}$ and 22 between 1.4 and 2.1 $M_{\odot}$. These candidates provide valuable targets for future follow-up observations and Gaia DR4 analyses. We also flag 1,317 additional potential compact binary candidates with effective RV epochs less than three, including 84 with inferred companion masses above 2.1 $M_{\odot}$ and 173 between 1.4 and 2.1 $M_{\odot}$. More importantly, our results point to a large, currently hidden population of black hole and neutron star binaries that can be further explored with the forthcoming Gaia DR4 data and complementary follow-up observations.

entries.title: The anomalously large transiting planet around Boyajian's star: evidence for a circumplanetary ring
entries.abstract: A recent study reported a transiting giant-planet candidate with a mass of $9.4^{+4.9}_{-4.1}\,M_{\rm J}$ and a radius of $1.7\pm0.1\,R_{\rm J}$ on a wide orbit around Boyajian's star (KIC 8462852, also called Tabby's star), which is well known for its irregular, deep flux dips. The reported radius is puzzling, because cool giant planets of $\sim$10\,$M_{\rm Jup}$ are expected to have radii close to Jupiter's, so the companion appears $\sim$60--70\% larger than standard models allow. Here we explore the solution that the planet is actually ringed. We develop a fast and accurate code to compute the transit light curve due to a ringed planet, and apply it to the TESS light curve. The ring model is marginally favoured by the data by $Δχ^2>10$ and a difference in Bayesian information criterion (BIC) of $<2$. The preferred configuration is a Jupiter-sized ($1.1\,R_{\rm J}$) planet surrounded by an opaque, highly flattened ring extending to $3.1$--$4.4$ planetary radii with a nearly polar obliquity. While the ring geometry is uncertain, simple estimates suggest that a debris annulus extending out to the planet's Roche limit is needed to explain the large transit depth. The ring thus removes the radius anomaly altogether and is qualitatively consistent with the dusty, comet-shepherding environment inferred from the star's historic dimmings.

entries.title: EP251129a: A Fast X-ray Transient with Two X-Ray Plateaus and Its Off-axis Afterglow
entries.abstract: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) detected by the Einstein Probe are extending the parameter space of relativistic stellar explosions toward softer and longer-lived transients. Here we report EP251129a/GRB 251129A at z=0.505, which exhibits two X-ray plateaus: an early plateau lasting $\sim 10^{4}\,\rm s$ followed by a rapid decay with spectral softening, and a second plateau extending to 60 days, placing it at the extreme long-duration end of Gamma Ray Burst (GRB) plateaus. The early optical emission evolves independently of the X-ray, indicating a different origin; whereas the unusual radio afterglow shows a rapid rise of $F_ν\propto t^{1.9-2.5}$ and a delayed peak at $\sim36-40$ days, providing strong evidence for an off-axis geometry. We find that the early X-ray behavior resembles those of ultra-long GRBs (ULGRBs) and can be naturally explained by the internal dissipation from a newborn millisecond magnetar undergoing gravitational-wave-dominated spin-down before collapsing into a black hole. The early optical, radio and late X-ray emission are well described by an off-axis two-component jet afterglow with additional energy injection, possibly powered by fallback accretion onto black hole. EP251129a therefore connects the emerging EFXT population with ULGRB-like central-engine activity and off-axis afterglow, offering a rare opportunity to probe both the evolution of central engine and jet structure in a single event.

entries.title: A frequency-resolved measurement of the scattering law in FRB 20210415C
entries.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) show diverse temporal morphologies, shaped both by their intrinsic emission and by propagation effects such as residual dispersion and multipath scattering. Because several of these effects can broaden a burst asymmetrically, an asymmetric profile does not by itself establish multipath scattering. We measure the frequency dependence of the temporal tail in FRB 20210415C, a bright burst from the repeating source FRB 20210219C. The burst is detected across approximately 400-800 MHz. Frequency-resolved fits yield an empirical exponential-tail timescale, $τ_{\rm emp}$, that follows $τ_{\rm emp}\proptoν^α$. Two complementary treatments of the underlying pulse width give $α=-3.95\pm0.07$ and $-4.14\pm0.08$. Both results are consistent with the commonly adopted $ν^{-4}$ scattering law. The inferred scattering time is approximately 8.0 ms at 583 MHz, exceeding Galactic foreground estimates by a factor of at least $4\times10^{2}$. This favours a dominant contribution beyond the Milky Way, although the data do not localise the scattering screen. FRB 20210415C therefore provides a direct measurement of a scattering law commonly imposed in catalogue analyses.

entries.title: Power spectrum of longitudinal-velocity residuals in the Galactic disk from Gaia DR3 red-giant-branch stars
entries.abstract: Non-axisymmetric structures in the Galaxy produce coherent stellar motions in the Galactic disk. These motions are usually interpreted by assuming parameterized gravitational potentials or specific perturbation models, thereby entangling direct kinematic information with model-dependent assumptions. Using Gaia DR3 astrometry, we analyze the Galactic longitudinal-velocity residuals of nearly four million red-giant-branch stars over $-4 < X_h < 4\, \mathrm{kpc}$ and $-6 < Y_h < 6\, \mathrm{kpc}$ in the heliocentric region. We construct an empirical axisymmetric baseline without introducing any dynamical model, and compute the power spectrum of the residual velocity field. The spectrum exhibits a broad peak at spatial frequency of $f \simeq 0.12 - 0.22\, \mathrm{kpc}^{-1}$, corresponding to a scale of around $5-8\, \mathrm{kpc}$. The residual amplitude is sensitive to the adopted distance scale: inverse-parallax distances $d_\varpi$ yield a peak of around $16\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$, while the Bailer-Jones geometric distances $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$ yield around $12\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$. Minimizing the low-frequency power favors a solar radial motion of $U_\odot=10.8\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $d_\varpi$ and $U_\odot=10.4\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$. Collectively, the resulting spectrum establishes Gaia astrometry as a direct probe of disk-wide non-axisymmetric kinematics and provides quantitative targets for future dynamical modeling and interpretation.

entries.title: How Quickly Did the Giants Form? Constraining the Formation Timescales of Massive Quiescent Galaxies at Cosmic Noon Using Chemical Evolution Modelling
entries.abstract: Massive quiescent galaxies (MQGs; $M_\star \sim 10^{11} \, \mathrm{M_\odot}$) at cosmic noon ($z \sim 2$) host $α$-enhanced stellar populations ($\mathrm{[Mg/Fe]} \sim 0.4 - 0.5$) at near-solar [Fe/H], implying rapid formation histories that spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting alone constrains poorly. To determine the physical conditions and formation timescales that generate these abundances, we employ a one-zone chemical evolution model with nucleosynthetic yields calibrated against resolved stars in the Sculptor dwarf spheroidal. Comparing our model to a compilation of observed abundances, we find MQGs are consistent with rapid formation timescales of $Δt_\mathrm{SF} \sim 0.1 - 0.4 \, \mathrm{Gyr}$. The progenitors must sustain high star-formation efficiencies (approximately the molecular gas depletion time; $τ_\star \sim 0.05 \, \mathrm{Gyr}$) and retain most of their metal-enriched ejecta ($η\sim 0$), consistent with high-redshift dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs). However, our model favours moderately active progenitors with typical star-formation rates (SFRs) of $200-400 \, \mathrm{M_\odot \, yr^{-1}}$, matching recently identified `NIRCam-dark' galaxies more closely than the broader DSFG population. Sustained starbursts ($\mathrm{SFR} \gtrsim 1000 \, \mathrm{M_\odot \, yr}^{-1}$) are disfavoured, since they would form most stellar mass before significant SN Ia enrichment and underproduce the observed [Fe/H]. The same framework also reproduces the central abundances of local early-type galaxies over longer timescales ($Δt_\mathrm{SF} \sim 0.6 - 1 \, \mathrm{Gyr}$). Chemical abundances can therefore provide powerful constraints on the formation histories of MQGs, and incorporating them into SED-fitting routines will ensure inferred histories remain consistent with the observed chemistry.

entries.title: Multiplicity of Massive stars in the Milky Way (M3W). II. The brightest single O stars: variability and systemic velocities
entries.abstract: (ABRIDGED) M3W studies the dynamical properties of massive stars in the solar vicinity, such as their systemic velocities, which are affected by variability effects: pulsations, line infilling by wind and disks, and incomplete knowledge about the central wavelengths. We want to increase the accuracy of the O-stars systemic velocities. We establish how different wavelength regions are affected by variability, determine the thresholds for the detection of spectroscopic binarity, and obtain accurate central wavelengths including the effects of contamination, forbidden lines, and wind infilling. We analyse 41 apparently single bright O stars. We used multi-epoch HR LiLiMaRlin spectroscopy cleaned with UNWIND and stellar models computed with FASTWIND. The epoch spectra were cross-correlated to study their variability. The RVs were computed from (a) cross-correlation of H and He lines with FASTWIND models, (b) profile fitting of metallic lines, and (c) cross-correlation of the full spectrum with a template star. A comparison between the RV dispersions for different wavelength regions reveals different groups of stars in terms of variability: (a) non-SG slow rotators, (b) fast rotators, (c) SGs, and (d) Oe stars. This is a manifestation of the different role of pulsations, winds, and disks in RV variability. We determine RV dispersion thresholds for the detection of new SBs. We also use a FASTWIND grid to establish the effects of (a) the presence of He II lines close to Balmer lines, (b) the existence of forbidden components in two He I lines, and (c) wind infilling in the determination of accurate RVs. With all of that, we determined RVs for our 41 stars, checked their accuracy, and discovered significant differences with literature values. Our analysis has further revealed four SB1 systems unknown in the summer of 2025, one new SB2, two new Oe stars, and three new Onfp stars.

entries.title: Linking Detectable Tidal Features to Stellar Halo Growth: An Integrated Analysis of the Outskirts of Massive Early-type Galaxies
entries.abstract: Motivated by the finding that massive galaxies with tidal features (GwT) are preferentially found in low-density environments, one wonders whether this trend arises from enhanced debris survivability or from more active mass-assembly histories. If driven by the latter, structural signatures, such as more developed stellar halos, should also form through cumulative accretion. To address this, we analyze azimuthally averaged surface-brightness profiles of 436 massive early-type galaxies from the DESI Legacy Imaging Survey, comparing the median-stacked profiles of galaxies with tidal features to those without. We find that, after resampling by stellar mass and environmental density, a subtle but systematic structural divergence emerges in the galaxy outskirts ($r>5\times r_{50}$). Specifically, the GwT population in the lower-density & higher-mass regime exhibits a relative intensity excess. This suggests that more developed stellar halos have formed, likely due to longer and/or more significant accretion events. In contrast, those in the higher-density & lower-mass regime show a relative deficiency in intensity, which is reasonable to interpret as a result of structural disruption from environmental effects rather than a lack of cumulative accretion. Our findings suggest that visible tidal features$-$particularly in massive systems within quiet environments$-$do not merely reflect recent stochastic accretion events but also hint at the long-term assembly history of galaxies. This work is a depth-limited study that offers a glimpse into an integrated analysis of tidal debris and stellar halos, thereby introducing a novel pathway to unravel the complex assembly histories of galaxies.

entries.title: An extended red wing of the 5797 Å diffuse interstellar band in the Red Rectangle nebula
entries.abstract: Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are interstellar molecular absorption features that are ubiquitous in the interstellar medium (ISM). So far, there was only one known sight line where DIBs show an extend tail towards the red (ETR), namely Herschel 36. Such sight lines are essential to illuminate the DIB problem, namely the identification of their carriers, because they show more DIB variation than standard ISM sight lines. To report a new detection of the 5797 Å DIB in the Red Rectangle nebula with an ETR, which adds a new observational constraint for the DIB carrier. We analysed archival GIRAFFE/FLAMES integral field spectroscopy to extract all spectral features between 5776 and 5810 Å at different spatial positions. We used time series spectra to identify stellar and circumstellar features, and data from different instruments to exclude instrumental effects. We report the firm detection of the 5797 Å DIB that is localised in the Red Rectangle nebula, or in the ISM in the sight line towards it. Curiously, while the 5797 Å DIB shows an ETR in the Red Rectangle, the 5780 Å DIB does not. Further, we report an exceptionally high equivalent ratio of EW(5797)/EW(5780) = 1.79 higher than any other literature value.

entries.title: Comparison of Hybrid and Standard Reconstruction Methods on IXPE Astrophysical Data
entries.abstract: The hybrid reconstruction algorithm developed by Cibrario et al. 2023 combined a convolutional neural network (CNN) with standard moment analysis to improve track reconstruction in IXPE Gas Pixel Detectors. Although validated on laboratory data (Cibrario et al. 2025), the method's astrophysical performance had not been systematically characterized. We present the first comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction on IXPE point sources, measuring sensitivity gains versus energy. We analyze Her X-1, a bright, polarized accreting pulsar as a benchmark, and soft-state XTE J1701-461, a bright neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary with no detected polarization, to assess residual systematics. From both pipelines' Level-2 event files, we compare normalized Stokes parameters, polarization degree (PD) and angle (PA), and detection significance. For Her X-1, hybrid reconstruction increases significance at all energies, significantly above ~2.83 keV. R = σ_hyb/σ_std differs from unity by 9.3σ in the 2.83-4.00 keV bin and reaches 1.18\pm0.03 at 5.66-8.00 keV (6.2σ). For XTE J1701-461, PD is consistent with zero and R with unity. Fourier analysis reveals excess power in hybrid angle distributions at low energies for modes m = 3, 6, 12 and 15, significant at >7σ relative to the standard method; at 5-8 keV, all modes are consistent with noise in both methods. These CNN-amplified hexagonal-grid artifacts do not affect Stokes parameters because they are orthogonal to polarization modes.The method delivers a statistically significant sensitivity gain for Her X-1, consistent with Cibrario et al. 2025 and equivalent to ~20% more effective area without extra observing time. These results support systematic use of hybrid reconstruction on IXPE astrophysical data.

entries.title: SoFTg: A hybrid segmentation framework for solar granulation revealing turbulent convection statistics at DKIST scales
entries.abstract: In this work, we present Solar Feature Tracking: granules (SoFTg), a new hybrid algorithm within the SoFT library designed for the segmentation and tracking of solar granulation. By combining a heuristic approach based on a custom adaptive-thresholding technique with the speed and robustness of deep-learning methods, SoFTg provides a fast, reliable and user-friendly solution for granule segmentation, followed by the standard SoFT approach for tracking. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm's performance using multiple metrics and analyse the different stages of the processing pipeline. The method is tested on three datasets acquired with the Visible Broadband Imager operating in the red continuum at the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope in Maui, Hawaii. We present distributions of both the lifetime and equivalent diameter of the thousands of granules tracked, providing, for the first time, statistically robust evidence of turbulent convection at the spatial scales now accessible through the high-resolution imaging capabilities of DKIST.

entries.title: QED VI: Neutral hydrogen gas in supernova-driven galactic outflows
entries.abstract: Winds that eject mass from galactic discs regulate the growth of galaxies, and observations show that, at least within a few kpc of the disc, most of the mass flux is carried by neutral rather than ionized material. However, it has proven difficult for simulations of supernova-driven winds to reproduce this observation, leading to speculations that the bulk of the mass must be driven by radiation pressure or cosmic rays rather than supernovae. Here we report simulations of supernova-driven winds using the GPU-accelerated code QUOKKA that reach a resolution of $Δx = 1$ pc, significantly higher resolution and simulation volume than previous work. At this resolution the winds are dominated by neutral mass, with cloud sizes, masses and column densities broadly similar to those of the HI clouds in the Milky Way's nuclear wind. The neutral material is not ballistic, but is instead driven by momentum transfer associated with drag and condensation of hot gas onto the neutral phase. By contrast, when we coarsen the resolution to values comparable to those used in earlier work, the neutral outflow weakens at $Δx = 2$ pc and disappears at $Δx = 4$ pc. We argue that this difference arises partly because lower-resolution simulations do not resolve, with a few cells, the 3-6 pc thick cooling layers in which hot gas condenses onto neutral clouds.

entries.title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing
entries.abstract: In canonical twisted-torus models of hydromagnetic equilibrium in neutron stars, the toroidal field is confined to regions where the poloidal field lines are closed. As spindown torques applied at the stellar surface need not be communicated efficiently to such magnetically-unlocked regions, toroidal zones or magnetic voids may rotate faster than the electromagnetically braked part of the star. Continuous gravitational radiation from the associated non-corotating quadrupole may therefore be emitted at higher frequencies than poloidal ones to a degree that depends on the diffusive microphysics controlling angular momentum transport. Dissipative processes can suppress long-lived lags, and we estimate the relevant timescales and their sensitivity to microphysics. Nevertheless, we show that a quadrupole component whose pattern speed differs from the observed spin is shifted, or smeared, over a finite frequency band. Single-template or narrowband upper limits therefore constrain only the quadrupole contribution lying inside the searched frequency window, not necessarily the full frequency-integrated quadrupole. Using simple models, we quantify this spectral redistribution over finite observation windows and discuss its implications for continuous-wave searches.

entries.title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and neutrino opacities in hot dense matter
entries.abstract:
We calculated the diffusion mean free paths of electron neutrinos and antineutrinos in hot, neutrino-trapped matter containing $Δ(1232)$ isobars, as found in proto-neutron stars and neutron star merger remnants. We included charged-current absorption with the $NΔ$ weak vertex of weak pion production, neutral-current scattering on all baryons and three-body antineutrino absorption on electron--baryon pairs, with relativistic mean-field kinematics. The reaction $ arν_e+e^-+n	oΔ^-$ dominates the antineutrino opacity whenever the neutron and electron chemical potentials exceed the in-medium $Δ^-$ rest energy, even where the $Δ$ population is negligible. At two to four times saturation density, where the reaction is open, it shortens the antineutrino mean free path from 
ubarLamNucMin--
ubarLamNucMax~m to 
ubarLamDMin--
ubarLamDMax~cm. Because antineutrinos are scarce at high lepton fraction, this changes lepton-number diffusion only at low lepton fraction, by up to \DtwoRedHi\% at these densities and by a factor of \DtwoRedLow\ at 1.5 times saturation density. For electron neutrinos, absorption on the $Δ^-$ and, at low lepton fraction, the opening of nucleonic absorption shorten the mean free path by factors of up to 
uRatioYLthreeMax\ at lepton fraction 0.3 and up to about 
uRatioYLoneMax\ at lepton fraction 0.1. We also showed that, for a given axial coupling, the spin of the $Δ$ reduces its Gamow--Teller strength per particle from 3 to $5/3$.

entries.title: The biases caused by interpolated table models and their impact on X-ray spectroscopy
entries.abstract: Models for X-ray spectroscopy involving complex relativistic or plasma physics are commonly pre-computed on a grid, In this paper, we aim to quantify the potential biases and distortions introduced by the computational error and propagated into parameter inference by interpolating linearly these complex, non-linear models. We analyse the performance of Bayesian sampling algorithms on mock inference problems. Then, we model real observations of an accreting black hole X-ray binary in both the soft and hard states. We find that linear interpolation can a) greatly bias the posterior distribution of model parameters and b) distort the likelihood space to such a degree that posterior distributions become artificially multimodal. This multi-modality causes a noticeable loss in computational efficiency in both sampling and fitting techniques. As a result, exploring a given parameter space until convergence requires an extremely large computational cost. These findings call for improving the computational techniques used when fitting modern X-ray data, for example through better sampling algorithms and/or more sophisticated interpolation schemes

entries.title: Investigating supernova-remnant X-ray maps with dendrogram-based techniques
entries.abstract: X-ray images of supernova remnants provide important information regarding the spatial distribution of the physical and chemical parameters of the shocked plasma. Our objective is to provide a comprehensive and quantitative assessment of the similarities observed across narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a given supernova remnant. We also aim to perform comparative analyses between distinct remnants. We adopted two dendrogram-based techniques, namely a multivariate analysis and a deep-learning, graph-based approach (by exploring different metrics) for the study of Chandra X-ray maps of Cassiopeia A, G292.0+1.8, Tycho's SNR, Kepler's SNR, and W49B. We also tested the reliability of our results on synthetic X-ray maps produced from a 3D hydrodynamic simulation of Cassiopeia A. We identify clusters of narrow-band images (and equivalent-width maps) corresponding to emission lines of chemical elements that are expected to be synthesized in the same layers of the exploding star and/or that originate from plasma at similar temperatures. By comparing different objects, we clearly observe strong similarities among Type Ia remnants (namely Tycho's SNR and Kepler's SNR) and core-collapse remnants (Cassiopeia A and G292.0+1.8), with W49B being more similar to the latter objects. The methodology developed in this work provides a robust tool to measure the analogies and differences between narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a supernova remnant, offering clues on the distribution of the different chemical species and on the plasma temperature. Although tested on a limited sample of objects, the adoption of this tool for the classification of supernova remnants (Type Ia vs. core-collapse) yields promising results.

entries.title: Photometric Redshift Estimation with Hybrid Quantum Neural Network
entries.abstract: A Hybrid Quantum Neural Network (HQNN) is applied to recover the photometric redshift of a galaxy dataset built using data from two astronomical surveys, the Kilo-Degree Survey (KIDS) and the VISTA Kilo-Degree Infrared Galaxy (VIKING), which provide data with coverage from the optical to the near-infrared electromagnetic spectrum. The results are then compared with those obtained by a classical neural network. We see that HQNN consistently recovers the reference photometric redshift with a high statistical fidelity. Furthermore, both the $R^2$ and the MSE found by the HQNN are consistently better than those found by the classical counterpart (albeit consistent in the error range), proving the worth of further investigating these novel technologies for this particular astrophysical application.

entries.title: Reconstructing the Three-Dimensional Stellar Mass Profiles of Massive Galaxy Clusters
entries.abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional (3D) stellar mass profiles of galaxy clusters using simulations and observations. We develop the Projection-to-Enclosed Estimator by Layers (PEEL) model, which geometrically reconstructs the 3D stellar mass profile from the projected stellar mass profile under the assumption of spherical symmetry. Starting from the outermost annulus, the PEEL model subtracts the contributions of the outer shells from the projected mass in each inner annulus. Using 205 halos from the TNG-Cluster simulation, we show that the reconstructed profile (hereafter the PEEL profile) recovers the true 3D stellar mass profile without systematic bias. We also examine potential systematic effects, including the use of subhalos versus stellar particles, the choice of cluster center, and the 3D shape of the halo. We then apply the PEEL model to a stacked sample of nine massive clusters from the MAssive Cluster survey with Hectospec (MACH). The observed PEEL profile is much flatter than the simulated 3D profile, indicating that the simulated clusters have a more centrally concentrated stellar mass distribution, mainly because of an excess of extremely massive galaxies in their cores. Combining the PEEL profile with the total mass profile from the caustic technique, we derive the stellar mass fraction profile of the observed clusters. The stellar mass fraction remains nearly constant at $0.009 \pm 0.002$ within $R_{200}$, consistent with previous observations and with the simulated clusters. The PEEL model provides a practical tool for measuring the 3D stellar mass profiles of large cluster samples from future wide-field spectroscopic surveys.

entries.title: NOEMA Observations of the Center of M33: A Parsec-scale Molecular Filament and an Ordered Gas-Star-Formation Sequence
entries.abstract: We present NOEMA CO(1-0) observations of the inner $\sim$500 pc of M33 at a resolution of $0.91''\times0.37''$ ($3.7\times1.5$ pc), resolving the compact molecular gas structures and revealing their relation to recent massive star formation. The most prominent structure is a southeastern molecular filament (SE filament) that extends 76 pc along its principal axis, is 23 pc wide, and contains three CO-bright knots. Across eight independent transverse cuts, the adjacent H$α$ ridge is displaced preferentially to one side of the principal CO ridge by a median $10.0^{+0.9}_{-1.4}$ pc. Young OB candidates are more closely associated with H$α$ than with compact CO. The filament shows little velocity change along its length but a resolved gradient across its minor axis. Its elongated morphology, transverse kinematics, and ordered CO-H$α$ distribution are consistent with locally asymmetric molecular-gas compression and subsequent massive star formation. Across the wider field, 23 well-measured compact clumps have a median radius of 2.67 pc and a median velocity dispersion of 2.15 km s$^{-1}$. Their linewidth and apparent virial-parameter distributions show no clear difference between the SE filament and the rest of the field. Although the local spiral potential and pattern speed remain unconstrained, the observations provide a resolved view of a compression-compatible molecular-to-ionized-gas sequence in the center of M33.

entries.title: Inferring the Total Mass of Galaxy Halos Using Photometry
entries.abstract: Galaxy size, as defined as the radius at which the stellar surface density reaches $1~\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-2}$ ($R_1$), has been shown to correlate more tightly with stellar mass than the effective radius. Cosmological simulations further predict a tight relation between $R_1$ and dark matter halo mass ($M_{200}$), but this prediction has not yet been tested observationally. We present the first observational test of the predicted $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation and assess whether galaxy size, defined through $R_1$, can serve as a robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. We analyze galaxies from the SPARC database, combining high-quality rotation curves to infer dark matter halo masses with stellar surface density profiles derived from photometric data to measure $R_1$. We then compare the observed relation with the predictions from state-of-the-art cosmological simulations. We find good agreement between observations and simulations: galaxies follow the same tight $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation predicted by numerical models across the explored mass range, with low intrinsic scatter. We provide the first observational validation of the $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation, demonstrating that $R_1$ is a simple, physically motivated, and robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. Because $R_1$ is determined entirely from photometric observations, it provides a tool for inferring halo masses from imaging data alone, with applications to studies of galaxy formation and evolution.

entries.title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons
entries.abstract: We revisit the supernova constraints on three well-motivated light gauge bosons: the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge boson. For the dark photon and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, we re-evaluate the nucleon bremsstrahlung process within the one-pion exchange approximation, retaining the full momentum and mass dependence. The geometrical dependence of the decay and absorption of these gauge bosons inside the supernova core is also taken into account. Updated bounds on these models are derived based on the cooling of SN1987A and energy deposition constraints from low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Taking the SFHo-18.8 $18.8\,M_\odot$ profile, the SN1987A cooling constraints reach masses of about $230$ MeV, $280$ MeV, and $300$ MeV for the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ boson, while the corresponding LESN limits extend to about $450$ MeV, $440$ MeV, and $600$ MeV, respectively. The kinetic mixing parameter $ε$ for dark photon, the gauge coupling $g_{BL}$ in the $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, and the gauge coupling $g_{μτ}$ for the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model are constrained down to $5.8\times10^{-12}$, $2.9\times10^{-16}$, and $6.4\times10^{-12}$, respectively.

entries.title: Nuclear fission: from fundamentals to frontiers
entries.abstract: Nuclear fission, the division of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter fragments, is a process of fundamental importance to nuclear physics, energy production, and the origin of the elements. This chapter, part of the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics, provides a pedagogical introduction to a broad array of topics in fission physics, progressing from the macroscopic liquid-drop model and microscopic shell corrections through fission dynamics, observables, modern theoretical frameworks, and experimental techniques ranging from traditional double-energy methods to inverse kinematics at radioactive-ion-beam facilities. The roles of fission in astrophysical nucleosynthesis, nuclear energy, medical isotope production, and national security are discussed, and open questions including the predictive power of microscopic theory and the fission properties of neutron-rich nuclei relevant to heavy element nucleosynthesis are highlighted.

entries.title: Parameter-Decoupling-Informed Learning for Superresolution: Laboratory Validation and Galaxy Imaging
entries.abstract: We present a parameter-decoupling-informed learning model for estimating subwavelength separations of point sources, without requiring prior knowledge of source properties, control over the sources, or continued access to their light signals. The method builds on our parameter-decoupled quantum superresolution estimation theory, which circumvents the need to estimate nuisance parameters such as partial coherence, brightness imbalance, and relative phase. Our convolutional neural network further accommodates practical imperfections, including background noise, photon loss, and centroid and orientation misalignment. We validate the method using synthetic and experimentally generated images, achieving separation-estimation fidelity above $82\%$ for separations as small as approximately $0.075σ$, where $σ$ is the Gaussian intensity-PSF standard deviation. This corresponds to an illustrative separation of $\sim13.5$ nm when $σ=180$ nm, suggesting potential relevance to length scales addressed by advanced active-source microscopy. Applied to archival Hubble images of NGC~4486B, the model yields nuclear separations of 9.3-13.2~pc, consistent with the previously reported value of 12~pc. Comparisons using the same training and testing images demonstrate substantially higher fidelity than conventional direct data-driven learning in the tested cases. The method's robustness to varying source properties and imaging imperfections supports retrospective astrophysical image analysis and motivates applications in live-cell microscopy and quantum metrology where source control or renewed optical measurements are impractical.

entries.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
entries.abstract: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

entries.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
entries.abstract: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

entries.title: Physical assumptions versus nature: the shape of the heliosphere
entries.abstract: Context. The Interstellar Probe study describes a mission concept with a launch window beginning in 2036, aiming to reach several hundred astronomical units beyond the heliopause within a time frame of at least 50 years. One of the fundamental questions related to this mission is where the boundaries of the heliosphere are and how thick they are. To answer it we need to know the shape of the heliosphere. Over the past 60 years numerous models of the heliosphere have been developed. For a long time these models depicted a heliosphere resembling a comet. Since around 2015 models have been presented that differ significantly from the shape of a comet. Aims. The aim of this paper is to emphasize that the obtained image of the heliosphere depends on the model assumptions contained in these articles. Methods. We review numerous publications examining the shape of the heliosphere. All of these articles use a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) model of the heliosphere together with various assumptions that simplify the physics of the interaction of the solar wind flowing from the Sun with the surrounding interstellar medium. Results. The result of all these studies is a shape of the heliosphere described as either croissant-like or cometary-like, depending on the assumptions made. Conclusions. We are still uncertain which model represents the real heliosphere. Nature requires a theoretical model that is more accurate. In our opinion the interaction of the solar wind with the interstellar medium must be described by the Boltzmann system of equations using artificial intelligence. In the context of the planned space mission this conclusion is crucial.

entries.title: An Intermediate Mass Stripped Star in a 4.2-hour Orbit around a Compact Object
entries.abstract: From their discovery as radio pulsars to landmark multi-messenger observations of their mergers, double neutron stars have transformed our understanding of the extreme Universe and the formation of heavy elements (Drout et al. 2017; Abbott et al. 2017). Yet, uncertainties in their formation result in predicted merger rates spanning orders of magnitude (Tauris et al. 2017; Mandel & Broekgaarden 2022). The most critical stage occurs when a star is stripped of its hydrogen-rich envelope, causing the binary orbit to shrink drastically. Despite its fundamental role, the resulting tight binaries comprising a stripped star and neutron star have remained elusive. Here we report a $\sim$$3.4\,M_{\odot}$ stripped star (Ludwig et al. 2026; Drout et al. 2023; Götberg et al. 2023) orbiting an unseen companion every 4.2 hours. Our orbital and spectroscopic analysis excludes a normal star, which would not fit within the orbit, as well as a second stripped star which would have been detectable in our spectra. Adding constraints from high cadence photometry gives a 99.4% probability that the companion is too massive to be a white dwarf, making a neutron star the most likely companion. We model the system's future and predict that the stripped star will transfer mass again before exploding as a hydrogen-free supernova, leaving a bound pair of neutron stars that will merge after 220 Myr. This system reveals a previously unconstrained phase of binary evolution, uncovering a new class of systems that probes the uncertain physics of massive stars, linking to observable gravitational-wave sources.

entries.title: Explainable Prediction of High-Speed Solar Wind Streams driven by Coronal Holes via Topological Data Analysis
