entries.abstract: High-speed solar wind streams (HSSs) originating from coronal holes (CHs) are an important driver of recurrent geomagnetic activity. Since HSSs are associated to coronal structures visible in extreme-ultraviolet observations, this provides a natural basis for forecasting several days in advance. In this work, we investigate whether the topology of coronal structures observed in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) images contains predictive information on the subsequent occurrence of CH-driven HSSs at Earth. To this end, we consider Topological Data Analysis (TDA), and in particular persistent homology, to classify EUV solar images according to the occurrence of HSSs at Earth four days later. The target is a binary classification of HSS occurrence at a four-day lead time, defined using an HSS interval catalog and solar wind speed thresholds. Several combinations of topological representations and classifiers are evaluated under a common cross-validation framework. The results indicate that the topology of EUV coronal structures alone contains predictive information on subsequent CH-driven HSS occurrence, despite the absence of explicit CH geometric descriptors in the model input. To investigate the origin of this predictive information, we develop a model-level explainability framework based on cross-validation-aggregated feature weights and spatial evidence maps. A fully traced example connects persistence diagrams and persistence-image features to the classifier output and to their spatial localization in the original EUV observation. The proposed framework provides a transparent and computationally lightweight approach for investigating the relationship between coronal topology and subsequent high-speed solar wind streams.

entries.title: The mass discrepancy problem in massive stars: an inferential perspective
entries.abstract: Bayesian inference has become a standard tool for inferring stellar parameters from stellar evolution models. However, comparatively little attention has been paid to how alternative Bayesian likelihood formulations influence inferred stellar parameters, and the resulting evolutionary mass discrepancy for massive main sequence stars. Here, we investigate the effects of mixing and alternative Bayesian likelihood formulations on the inferred stellar parameters and the resulting evolutionary mass discrepancy. We analysed a sample of seven double-lined eclipsing B type binaries with $β$ Cep components using one pre-computed MESA grid of stellar evolution models and observables such as mass, effective temperature, surface gravity and luminosity. Stellar parameters were inferred within a Bayesian inference method employing nested sampling and piecewise cubic interpolation across the model grid. We compared several inference strategies, including single-star and coeval binary models, with and without dynamical masses included in the likelihood function. Bayesian evidence and Pareto-optimal model selection were used to evaluate the preferred solutions. Our work reinforces that core-boundary mixing is required for all stars. Further, the inferential analysis demonstrates that different likelihood formulations may lead to systematically different inferred mass discrepancies. For the adopted input physics and the small sample of stars, we find that about half of the apparent reduction in the inferred mass discrepancy may arise from the construction of the Bayesian likelihood, while enhanced near-core mixing accounts for the remaining improvement. The preferred coeval solutions further indicate that the systems span central hydrogen mass fraction of $0.632$ -- $0.205$, with ages of $4.25$ -- $12.27$ $\rm Myr$ determined with precisions of $2$ -- $13\%$ under the adopted model input physics.

entries.title: SPAM: Survey Overview and JWST/NIRCam Multi-Band Photometry Catalog
entries.abstract: We present the Star-formation from Photometry through the Addition of Medium-bands (SPAM) survey, a 62.9 hr JWST/NIRCam imaging program to add ten new filters, nine medium-band filters, and one broad-band filter to the CEERS legacy dataset. We describe the observation strategy, present the data, and detail the data-reduction process. We include a complete reduction of imaging in the legacy CEERS footprint, inclusive of all publicly available photometric parallel and GO observations within the legacy CEERS footprint. We present a multi-band photometric and photometric redshift catalog which includes all medium- and broad-band filters available on NIRCam. We find that adding medium bands from the SPAM and MINERVA programs improves photometric redshifts. We discuss how these data advance the SPAM survey's key science goals: better-constrained photometric redshifts, identification of high-redshift overdensity members, improved recovery of emission-line strengths, and more accurate star formation histories.

entries.title: Classification of Fermi Blazars of Uncertain Type Using Positive-Unlabelled Machine Learning
entries.abstract: We apply positive-unlabelled (PU) machine learning to the 1623 blazars of uncertain type (BCUs) in the Fermi Large Area Telescope Fourth Source Catalogue, Data Release 4 (4FGL-DR4). Five PU classifiers are trained on seven gamma-ray features, once with the 820 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) and once with the 1490 BL Lac objects as the labelled class (FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode). Each source is scored out of fold over 100 repeated five-fold splits, and its confidence is the fraction of splits in which at least three of the five classifiers flag it. At a confidence of at least 0.1, 437 BCUs are FSRQ-like, 597 are BL Lac-like, 12 are flagged in both modes and 577 in neither. On known sources the ensemble reaches a recall of 0.80 in FSRQ mode and 0.82 in BL Lac mode at a false-positive rate of 0.08, but a logistic regression trained on the labelled sources alone does at least as well, so PU learning gives no accuracy gain here. Removing the sky coordinates from the features does not lower the performance on known sources but adds 107 BCUs to the candidate lists and drops 30, which is consistent with the coordinates acting as a selection shortcut, so we exclude them. We check the candidates against published optical spectra, SDSS-V spectra, and BCUs that later received a class in the catalogue. Among sources assigned a single class, BL Lac-like calls are correct for 84 to 100% of the sources and FSRQ-like calls for 58 to 83%, depending on the sample. These samples come from spectroscopic follow-up and do not represent all BCUs. The candidates are fainter and lie closer to the Galactic plane than the labelled sources, and the excess of unclassified BCUs in the plane is not explained. We release the confidences of all 1623 BCUs.

entries.title: Gravitationally Induced Polarization-Angle Rotation in Pulsar-Black Hole Binaries
entries.abstract: Radio pulsars emit highly polarized radiation whose polarization properties are commonly described by the Rotating Vector Model (RVM). In this work, we investigate the effects of gravitational light bending and parallel transport on the polarization profile of a pulsar in a hypothetical binary system with a black hole (BH) companion. We combine the RVM with numerical integration of null geodesics to calculate the polarization direction along the photon trajectory and model the orbital-phase-dependent variation of the observed polarization position angle (PPA). We consider both non-spinning and spinning black hole companions and include the evolution of the orbital geometry due to relativistic spin-orbit coupling. For a non-spinning black hole, the change in the observed polarization direction arises from the geometric shift associated with gravitational light bending. For a spinning black hole, frame dragging introduces an additional geometric shift, while parallel transport produces an additional polarization rotation measured relative to our chosen reference construction. We investigate the dependence of these polarization changes on the binary parameters and the orientation of the pulsar spin. We find that gravitational light bending can significantly distort the characteristic S-shaped PPA profile, particularly near superior conjunction, and can reverse its overall sense of variation for the supermassive black hole system considered here. Relativistic spin-orbit evolution also affects the orbital-phase dependence of the polarization profile, particularly in the supermassive black hole system. These results show that relativistic photon propagation can modify both the shape and the phase dependence of pulsar polarization profiles and may provide a useful probe of the geometry of pulsar-BH binaries when such systems are discovered.

entries.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
entries.abstract: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

entries.title: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
entries.abstract: We report an indication of $\barν_e$ from the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB) based on a spectral fit analysis of a 5003.0-day dataset in Super-Kamiokande. Key improvements over previous searches include enhanced rejection of atmospheric $ν$ backgrounds, updated evaluations of systematic uncertainties, and a refined spectral fitting method. Using a representative DSNB model, the best-fit flux was determined to be $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ for $E_ν>13.3$~MeV, corresponding to a $2.6σ$ tension with a null hypothesis ($99.5\%$ C.L., one-sided). Similar significances were obtained with signal models of varying spectral shapes.

entries.title: The long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus: a comparison between GRMHD simulations and relativistic thin disk theory
entries.abstract: In this paper we analyse the long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus using novel GRMHD simulations which, for the first time, have been run out to extremely large evolutionary times $t_{\rm max} = 10^7 GM_\bullet/c^3$. This allows for detailed comparisons between the gross evolution of this GRMHD simulation and existing "spreading disk" analytical theories. We show that the long-term features of this evolution are well described by General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory (GRTDT), which reproduces various aspects of the GRMHD evolution to within a factor $\sim 2$, despite the disk in our simulation not being remotely thin, showing dynamically dominant (MAD) magnetic fields, and launching a powerful wind. Thin disk theory functions as an accurate and cheap effective theory for the evolution in radius and time of the bulk of the disk material, and for the time dependence of the horizon accretion rate. We argue that this effectiveness originates from the global conservation laws of mass and angular momentum, together with a turbulent stress which we find to be local and independent of density, lending support to the ad-hoc local-stress-tensor phenomenology employed in analytical models. We also find that the turbulent accretion rate variability in the inner disk is log-normally distributed, consistent with a key assumption in the modeling of observed variability.

entries.title: Constraining Supermassive Black Hole Seeding and Accretion via Occupation Fractions and Mass-Weighted Distributions
entries.abstract: The formation of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is a key open problem in galaxy evolution, with light- and heavy-seeding models predicting distinct black hole occupation fractions (BHOFs). Using multiwavelength observations from the LSST Deep Drilling Fields, we measure the AGN fraction and estimate the BHOF across $0<z<1$. Applying a hierarchical Bayesian model, we find that the inferred BHOF remains $100\%$ for host galaxy masses below $10^9 M_\odot$ at lower redshifts. These findings are consistent with light-seed scenarios. Additionally, we computed the black hole masses for several galaxies in the W-CDF-S to test the mass-weighted black hole occupation distributions from semi-analytic models (SAM). Using a reduced-$χ^2$ analysis, we find that the data are consistent with the main-sequence accretion model regardless of the assumed seeding mechanism. These results provide new observational constraints on SMBH seeding and highlight the value of combining deep extragalactic surveys with probabilistic modeling.

entries.title: The design and flight of the Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations (PUEO)
entries.abstract: Sources of cosmic rays at ultrahigh energies (UHE, $\gtrsim$ 1 EeV) are anticipated to give rise to neutrinos at similar energies by production via propagation interactions either within the source region or on cosmological scales. Measurements of the neutrino flux, flavor, and energy provide significant insight into those underlying processes governing UHE cosmic ray acceleration and propagation. Detecting neutrinos at these energies requires immense detector volumes due to their low predicted flux. We present the balloon-borne mission PUEO (Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations) which is an antenna array designed to detect the Askaryan emission from UHE neutrino interactions in the Antarctic ice. This paper reports on the design considerations and implementations for constructing PUEO, from the design parameters to the as-built validations.

entries.title: Connectivity rewiring and filament formation by active region emergence observed with Solar Orbiter
entries.abstract: Using an 11-day dataset from Solar Orbiter, combining EUV imaging, H$α$ observations, vector magnetograms and nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, we track the evolution from the emergence of a new active region to the reconfiguration of coronal connectivity. We find that the restructuring proceeds through a sequence of localized reconnection events that propagate along the filament channel, producing successive brightenings and bidirectional flows. This process leads to the gradual erosion of the original filament and the simultaneous formation of a new, highly sheared filament connecting the two regions. Magnetic modeling reveals a transition from a sheared arcade supporting the initial filament to a twisted flux rope underlying the newly formed structure. Our results demonstrate that flux emergence can reorganize filament channels through a spatially and temporally ordered sequence of reconnection events, rather than a single impulsive episode. This sequential reconnection front provides a natural mechanism for filament formation in evolving active regions and highlights the importance of continuously changing magnetic connectivity in the corona.

entries.title: Mapping the Milky Way with SDSS-V: Galactic Genesis Selection Function and Mock Catalog
entries.abstract: Robust chemodynamic mapping of the Milky Way requires accounting for the selection function of the survey used, the probability that a given star is included in the final catalog as a function of its observable properties. We derive the empirical selection function of the SDSS-V Galactic Genesis survey, the largest Milky Way Mapper program targeting red giant stars for Galactic structure studies. Treating the Galactic Genesis sample as a subsample of its 2MASS parent catalog, we model the selection function as a function of sky position, apparent H magnitude, and G-H color using a Bayesian binomial estimator, computing both a mean and maximum a posteriori (MAP) version. The resulting selection function reflects the survey's targeting strategy and observing history, including the transition from the pencil-beam SDSS-IV footprint to the fuller sky coverage of SDSS-V and the prioritization of the Magellanic Clouds. Using this selection function with the FIRE-2 Milky Way-mass simulations, we construct mock Galactic Genesis catalogs built on existing mock Gaia DR3 catalogs, injecting realistic photometric noise and applying the selection function via a per-star Bernoulli accept-reject procedure. We demonstrate the mock catalogs' utility with an example application to azimuthal metallicity variations in the disk. Furthermore, we release a Python package allowing users to recompute the selection function for their own samples and science cases. The package, selection function and mock catalogs will be updated and made available as the survey continues, extending the tools needed to reach the full scientific potential of SDSS-V Galactic Genesis.

entries.title: Tidal contributions to neutron star orbital precession around Sgr $A^*$
entries.abstract: We investigate tidal contributions to the orbital precession of neutron stars around the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, using stellar configurations described by the Tolman - Oppenheimer - Volkoff equations. We examine the dependence of tidal precession on stellar compactness, pericentre distance, and the quadrupolar tidal Love number $k_2$, and compare its magnitude with general relativistic orbital precession. The calculated tidal angular shift decreases strongly with increasing pericentre distance and, for the stellar configurations considered, with increasing compactness. Larger Love numbers enhance the tidal contribution. This behaviour reflects the strong dependence of tidal precession on the stellar-radius-to-pericentre-distance ratio, $(R/r_p)^5$. Despite the enhancement during closer encounters, the predicted tidal shifts remain extremely small, reaching approximately $3.5 \times 10^{-18},μas$ within the displayed parameter range. The ratio of tidal to general relativistic precession spans approximately $10^{-33}$ - $10^{-28}$, indicating that relativistic precession overwhelmingly dominates. Our results suggest that direct detection of the neutron-star tidal contribution through orbital precession around Sgr A* would be exceptionally challenging under the assumptions of the adopted model.

entries.title: The Impact of Flyby Interactions on the Rotation of Open Clusters
entries.abstract: The Gaia astrometric mission has provided the first evidence for the bulk rotation of open clusters. While this rotation may arise from residual spin inherited from a cluster's parent molecular cloud, it is unclear whether this explanation always suffices, as angular momentum is carried away by escaping stars on the timescale of two-body relaxation. In particular, the recent observance of significant rotation ($v_{\rm rot} = 0.81 \pm 0.06$ km s$^{-1}$) in the dynamically old ($\approx 4$ Gyr) open cluster M67 motivates a study of another potential source of spin for Solar neighborhood clusters: tidal torquing from gravitational encounters with passing giant molecular clouds (GMCs). We derive an analytic estimate for the change in angular momentum of a cluster due to an impulsive interaction with a passing GMC, and verify this expectation by performing $N$-body simulations over a range of encounter parameters using REBOUND. For highly energetic encounters, significant angular momentum can be transferred, but the stars that receive the most angular momentum are ejected, leaving the cluster remnant with negligible net rotation. Even when considering a random walk of many GMC-cluster encounters, the integrated effects of these interactions cannot explain observations of dynamically old rotating open clusters. However, we find that within $\sim 5$ Myr post-encounter, some disrupted clusters could be confused as rotating clusters while their stars are still dispersing. Using the local density of GMCs, we estimate that up to $\approx 1\%$ of open clusters in the Milky Way may carry this faux-rotation signal.

entries.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
entries.abstract: The interaction of strong ($a_0>1$), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by $\varepsilon_{\rm B}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm B}/ω_0$, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For $\varepsilon_{\rm B}<1$ the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency $Ω_{\rm B}$ to scattering; when $Ω_{\rm B}$ exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm p}^{-2/3}$ to $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm B}^{1/2}/\varepsilon_{\rm p}$ wavelengths ($\varepsilon_{\rm p}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm p}/ω_0$; $ω_{\rm p}$ is the plasma frequency). When $a_0^2>\varepsilon_{\rm B}>1$, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.

entries.title: Direct measurement of the ${}^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p, γ){}^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ reaction using the DRAGON recoil separator and a hybrid array of $γ$-ray detectors
entries.abstract: Background: The $^{23}$Mg$(p,γ)^{24}$Al reaction plays a key role in nova nucleosynthesis, serving as a bridge between the Ne-Na and Mg-Al cycles and impacting synthesis of a wide variety of nuclides. It is crucial that the rate of this reaction be well constrained by experimental data, in particular the properties of the key resonance at $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV, which dominates the rate at nova temperatures. Purpose: Our study aims to improve experimental constraints on the energy and strength of the key $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV $^{23}$Mg$(p,γ)^{24}$Al resonance through a new direct measurement of its strength and energy. Methods: We used a $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}$ radioactive beam to directly observe capture into the $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV resonance in inverse kinematics. The $^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ recoils were selected by the DRAGON recoil separator, and coincident $γ$ rays were measured in a hybrid $\mathrm{LaBr}_3/\mathrm{CeBr}_3/\mathrm{BGO}$ scintillator array. The $^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ singles yield was used to determine the resonance strength, while the time difference between the coincident $γ$ rays and the incident beam was used to determine the resonance energy. Results: We obtained a strength of $ωγ=38(7)$ meV and an energy of $E_{\mathrm{cm}}=478.8(26)$ keV for the key astrophysical $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p,γ)^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ resonance. Conclusions: Our reported strength is in excellent agreement with the previously reported direct measurement, as well as shell model calculations. Our energy is in good agreement with earlier indirect measurements. Reaction rate calculations incorporating our results indicate that the $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p,γ)^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ rate is constrained to a $1σ$ up/down factor of 1.5 or smaller in the nova temperature range of 0.2--0.4 GK.

analysis.reason: This study reports the spectroscopic confirmation of a strongly lensed stripped-envelope Type IIb supernova at $z = 1.276$, providing physical luminosity constraints and multi-messenger/cosmological lensing time-delay predictions relevant to massive star progenitor evolution.
analysis.result: SN Ares is spectroscopically classified as a Type IIb core-collapse supernova at $z_{\rm spec} = 1.276 \pm 0.002$ magnified by $\mu \approx 4.6 - 5.6$. Correcting for magnification (gain $\approx 1.9\;\mathrm{mag}$), its inferred intrinsic peak absolute magnitude is $M_{B,\max} \approx -17.1$ to $-17.9\;\mathrm{mag}$, consistent with binary progenitor systems like SN 1993J. Strong lensing modeling predicts two trailing images appearing $\sim 70-76\;\mathrm{yr}$ and $\sim 73-79\;\mathrm{yr}$ later.

analysis.reason: Wolf-Rayet stars are key progenitors of stripped-envelope supernovae and potential central-engine-driven transients; quantifying how stellar crowding systematically dilutes emission-line equivalent widths and distorts inferred mass-loss rates $\dot{M}(Z)$ is crucial for establishing pre-supernova circumstellar medium (CSM) density profiles.
analysis.result: In M33, approximately 27% (33/123) of WR stars suffer moderate-to-severe continuum dilution ($F_{\rm WR} < 0.85$, with very crowded sources having $F_{\rm WR} \lesssim 0.50$ and optical equivalent widths diluted by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$). Because optically thin recombination line luminosities scale as $L_{\rm line} \propto \dot{M}^{2}$, uncorrected dilution severely underestimates or distorts $\dot{M}$. Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopy confirms the predicted dilution (${\rm EW_{Hecto}/EW_{DEIMOS}} = 0.55\text{--}0.90$) and yields wind velocity diagnostics of $v_{\rm FWHM} \approx 330\text{--}1025\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ for $\mathrm{He\ II}$ and blue absorption edge velocities $v_{\rm blue} \approx 700\text{--}1500\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ for $\mathrm{He\ I}\,\lambda 5876$.
analysis.reading_entry: V.2 Implications for Wind Diagnostics and Mass-Loss Rates
analysis.problem: Ground-based fiber spectroscopy (e.g., MMT/Hectospec with $1\farcs 5$ fibers corresponding to $\sim 4\text{ pc}$ in M33) blends WR targets with surrounding OB stars and diffuse ISM, diluting diagnostic emission lines and contaminating wind mass-loss diagnostics across metallicity gradients.
analysis.method: Combined high-resolution ($0\farcs 1$) HST/PHATTER UV/optical photometry with a synthetic Gaussian fiber aperture model ($r_{\rm fib} = 0\farcs 75$, $\mathrm{FWHM} = 1\farcs 0$) to calculate the fractional WR flux contribution $F_i = \frac{f_i \cdot 10^{-0.4 m_i}}{\sum_j f_j \cdot 10^{-0.4 m_j}}$, established an empirical crowding metric based on centroid offset $d$ and magnitude difference $\Delta m_{12}$, and benchmarked ground spectra against narrow-slit Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopy.
limits: Crowding metric cannot uniquely identify WR counterparts in dense cluster cores like NGC 604 or very close binaries ($\Delta m_{12} \lesssim 0.5$ mag within $\lesssim 0\farcs 5$), where sub-arcsecond adaptive optics or IFU spectroscopy is required.

Spectra are continuum-normalized, offset vertically for clarity, and ordered by spectral subtype from earliest, hottest winds (bottom) to latest, coolest winds (top). Stellar wind features are marked with dotted lines and nebular emission features with dashed lines. The He II $\lambda 5411$ broad emission lines—one of the primary early WN diagnostics—are prominent in the WN and WNL objects but weaken significantly or vanish in the late-type Ofpe/WN9 stars. Conversely, the two Ofpe/WN9 stars (top) exhibit narrower emission profiles and significant He I features (notably the P Cygni profile at He I $\lambda 5876$) relative to the earlier WN subtype (bottom), consistent with their cooler, slower, and denser winds. The progression from broad, high-ionization features (WN) to narrow, low-ionization profiles (Ofpe/WN9) confirms the published WN classifications and, through reduced fiber contamination, enables quantitative wind diagnostics inaccessible from the original Hectospec data (§ IV.3, § IV.2 ).

analysis.reason: This paper presents an optical Fourier-domain spectroscopic method for detecting faint stellar companions to hot massive stars, which lacks substantial connection to high-energy transients, relativistic jets, FRB/PRS, or high-energy compact object observations.
analysis.result: The Fourier framework enables detection and rigorous upper limits on faint companions from single rotationally broadened lines. Applied to CPD$-41^\circ 7742$ ($V \simeq 8.3$), He~I $6678\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ yields companion detection with line-depth ratio $\hat{\alpha} = (24 \pm 2)\%$ (blind amplitude search, $\mathcal{T}=174$) and $\hat{\alpha} = (16 \pm 1)\%$ (phase search with orbital prior, $\mathcal{T}=169$), while companion-free He~II $5411\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ yields non-detections with $\hat{\alpha} < 2.1\%$ and $< 1.1\%$, respectively. Relative sensitivity scales as $\Delta\alpha/\alpha \propto v^{-\eta}$, with $\eta \approx 4$ for amplitude and $\eta \approx 1$ to $3$ for phase searches.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing genuine quiescent stellar-mass black holes from faint luminous stellar companions in massive binaries ($M \gtrsim 8\,M_\odot$), where rapid primary rotation ($v\sin i \sim 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) degrades radial-velocity and spectral disentangling sensitivity.
analysis.method: Transforming absorption line profiles into Fourier space where rotational and intrinsic Voigt broadenings act as smooth envelopes: $\ln|\tilde{S}| \simeq -\pi v_\gamma |\zeta| - \pi^2 [\frac{v_{\rm g}^2}{4\ln 2} - (\frac{\epsilon}{15}-\frac{1}{2})v_{\rm r}^2]\zeta^2 - \pi^4 [(\frac{1}{24}-\frac{\epsilon}{63})v_{\rm r}^4]\zeta^4 + \mathrm{const}$, and companion perturbations manifest as periodic modulations $\ln|\tilde{S}| \approx \ln|\tilde{U}^{(\textsc{a})}| + \alpha\cos(2\pi\zeta v)$ and $\arg(\tilde{S}_0) \approx -\alpha\sin(2\pi\zeta v)$. Detection is evaluated via the likelihood ratio statistic $\mathcal{T}=\max_v[\chi^2_{\textsc{h}_0}-\chi^2_{\textsc{h}_1}(v)]$ calibrated by injection-recovery tests.
limits: At small velocity separation ($v \to 0$), the companion signal degenerates with the smooth baseline, rendering line-depth ratio $\alpha$ unmeasurable.

analysis.reason: The paper develops an analytical scaling framework for the initial outer conditions of AGN accretion disks formed by the capture and disruption of strongly magnetized, cold ISM clouds. It systematically predicts magnetically dominated (low-$\beta$), toroidally stretched disks and super-Eddington accretion rates across mass ratios $M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl}$, providing valuable initial/boundary conditions for compact object accretion and relativistic jet generation.
analysis.result: The initial disk formed at the circularization radius $r_t$ is toroidally magnetically dominated with $\beta \ll 1$ and $|B_\phi| \gg |B_z|, |B_R|$. The disk scale height and accretion rate scale as $H_d/r_t \sim 4\alpha_{\rm cl,B}$ and $\dot{m} \sim 7\alpha_{\rm cl,B}(\Sigma_{\rm cl}/100\,M_\odot\,{\rm pc^{-2}})^{3/4}(M_{\rm cl}/10^7\,M_\odot)^{-1/4}(2/\tilde{v})$ for $M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$, where $\alpha_{\rm cl,B} \equiv E_{\rm mag}/E_{\rm grav}$. For $M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$, the tidal disruption gives $r_t \approx \xi(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl})^{1/3}R_{\rm cl}$ and $H_d/r_t \sim (3\alpha_{\rm cl,B})^{1/4}(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl})^{-1/4}$. In the post-encounter cutoff phase, the mass fallback follows a tidal-disruption-like power law $\dot{M} \propto t^{-5/3}$.
analysis.problem: Standard accretion disk models (e.g., Shakura-Sunyaev, classical Bondi, or TDE disks) assume initially thermal-pressure-dominated gas (high $\beta$) and weak or dynamically unimportant seed magnetic fields, failing to describe the realistic formation and structure of outer accretion disks fed by turbulent, strongly magnetized interstellar clouds.
analysis.method: Analytical formulation combining magnetic flux-freezing, supersonic turbulent energy conservation, and tidal disruption dynamics across three mass regimes ($M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm cl}$, $M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$, $M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$), evaluated with cloud mass functions $dN_{\rm cl}/dM_{\rm cl} \propto M_{\rm cl}^{-\gamma_{\rm cl}}$ and Larson scaling relations $v_{\rm cl} \propto R_{\rm cl}^{1/2}$.
assumptions: Interstellar clouds are strongly magnetized with initial plasma $\beta_{\rm cl} \ll 1$, supersonic turbulence, and rapid radiative cooling ($t_{\rm cool} \ll t_{\rm dyn}$).

analysis.reason: This paper investigates how dynamical tides and resonance locking between neutron star internal oscillation modes and orbiting sub-solar mass primordial black holes govern orbital evolution and modify pulsar timing observables.
analysis.result: Resonance locking modifies the orbital evolution according to $\frac{\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb}}{\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb}^{\rm GW}} = \frac{I_{\rm orb}}{I_{\rm orb}-3I_{\rm NS}}$. If $I_{\rm orb} > 3I_{\rm NS}$ and $\Omega_{\rm orb} > \Omega_{\rm NS}$, tidal torques accelerate inspiral; conversely, when $I_{\rm orb} < 3I_{\rm NS}$ and $\Omega_{\rm NS} > \Omega_{\rm orb}$, angular momentum extracted from the NS spin drives an outspiral ($\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb} < 0$), preventing coalescence. During resonance locking, the pulsar braking index shifts to $n = \frac{11I_{\rm orb} - 21I_{\rm NS}}{3(I_{\rm orb} - 3I_{\rm NS})} \frac{\Omega_{\rm NS}}{\Omega_{\rm orb}}$, yielding $n \to \frac{11}{3}\frac{\Omega_{\rm NS}}{\Omega_{\rm orb}}$ in the limit $I_{\rm orb} \gg 3I_{\rm NS}$. Gravitational-wave detectability exhibits a weak scaling ${\rm SNR} \propto \eta^{1/2}$, enabling Cosmic Explorer to detect $M_{\rm BH} > 10^{-6}\,M_\odot$ at $10\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ (${\rm SNR} > 10$).
analysis.reading_entry: Neutron Star–Primordial Black Hole Binaries: Dynamical Tides, Resonance Locking, and Gravitational Waves
analysis.problem: In extreme mass-ratio binaries with $M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm NS}$, standard equilibrium tides have negligible dissipation ($Q_{\rm tide} \gtrsim 10^3$, $\Omega_{\rm orb} t_{\rm tide} \sim 10^{16}$), leaving open the role of dynamical tides and mode resonance locks in driving or halting binary inspiral and altering pulsar braking indices.
analysis.method: Coupled orbital and rotational post-Newtonian equations are evaluated with dynamical tidal torque $\tau_{\rm tide}$ and gravitational-wave backreaction $\tau_{\rm GW}$. Low-frequency NS modes ($1\,\mathrm{Hz} \lesssim \omega_X/2\pi \lesssim 200\,\mathrm{Hz}$) are modeled with non-linear forcing $f_{\rm ext} = -2\gamma \dot{a}_X - \beta a_X^3$. In the slowly varying envelope approximation $a_X = c_X e^{i\omega_X t}$ with $c_X = R e^{i\theta}$, mode evolution is governed by $\dot{R} = -\gamma R + \frac{A_X}{2\omega_X}\sin(\theta - \delta\phi)$ and $\dot{\theta} = \frac{3\beta}{8\omega_X}R^2 + \frac{A_X}{2\omega_X R}\cos(\theta - \delta\phi)$, shifting the resonance frequency by $\omega_X' = \omega_X + \frac{3\beta}{8\omega_X}R^2$.

analysis.result: Magnetically driven outflows from MADs smoothly traverse slow-magnetosonic, Alfvén, and fast-magnetosonic critical points, attaining mildly relativistic velocities ($v_{\rm p} \gtrsim 0.1c - 0.3c$) from inner disc streamlines ($R \lesssim 20 R_{\rm in}$, where $R_{\rm in}=6R_{\rm g}=6GM/c^2$) with distinct radial velocity stratification. Owing to high magnetization and low mass loading, the dimensionless magnetic lever arm reaches $\tilde{l} = (R_{\rm A}/R)^2 \sim 10 - 100$, allowing an outflow mass-loss rate of $\dot{M}_{\rm w} \simeq 0.14 \dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ to remove roughly $55\%$ of the disc angular momentum ($J_{\rm w} \simeq 0.55 J_{\rm acc}$).
analysis.problem: Accounting for the acceleration and mass-loading of ultra-fast outflows (UFOs, $v \sim 0.1c-0.7c$) in highly ionized inner accretion flows around black holes where radiative line driving fails.
analysis.method: Steady, axisymmetric trans-magnetosonic MHD outflow framework along prescribed magnetic field surfaces $\Phi=[(R/R_{\rm in})^2+(1+|z/R_{\rm in}|)^2]^{1/2}-(1+|z/R_{\rm in}|)$ with polytropic equation of state $P=K\rho^\gamma$ ($\gamma=1.4, 1.5$), adopting disc surface boundary conditions calibrated from GRMHD MAD simulations (geometric thickness $H/R \simeq 0.3$, sub-Keplerian rotation $f_\Omega = \Omega/\Omega_{\rm K} < 1$, and magnetization $\beta_{z_{\rm h}} \lesssim 1$).

analysis.reason: This paper presents a relativistic 2D time-domain magnetoelastic simulation of magnetar crusts with dynamic failure ('plastic islands'), explaining the transient drift and cascading behavior of QPOs observed during magnetar bursts and giant flares.
analysis.result: Dynamic crustal failure leads to collective avalanches and slow creeping failures that multiply the failed volume fraction by a factor of $\approx 4$ (from $f_{\rm fail}(0) \approx 9\%$ to $f_{\rm fail} = 35.4\%$ for global quakes, and $0.6\%$ to $2.6\%$ for localized quakes with $E_{\rm kin,0}=7.07\times 10^{41}\text{ erg}$). Avalanching develops promptly within $\approx 8\text{ ms}$, accompanied by discrete QPO modes (e.g., $18.79, 24.01, 49.52\text{ Hz}$, and localized high-frequency modes at $\sim 113.5\text{ Hz}$) that drift over beat timescales $T_{\rm beat} \sim |\omega_1 - \omega_2|^{-1} \sim 1\text{ s}$. The failure volume scales non-monotonically with the poloidal field $B_p$ peaking around $B_p \sim 10^{14}\text{ G}$, and scales with kick efficiency as $\frac{f_{\rm fail}(50\text{ ms})}{f_{\rm fail}(0)} = 3.7 + 0.193\ln\eta$.
analysis.problem: Standard magnetar QPO models treat the crust as an elastic continuum that remains completely intact throughout oscillations, failing to account for dynamic yielding, plastic avalanching, and the resultant transient mode drifting observed in giant flare and burst tails.
analysis.method: Linearized Einstein-Maxwell-Euler axial perturbations are solved in the time domain under the Cowling approximation ($\delta g_{\mu\nu} = 0$) using a central leapfrog scheme with CFL parameter $C_{\rm CFL}=0.25$ and local wave speed $v_{\mu B}=[(\mu+B^{2}/4\pi)/(\epsilon+p+B^{2}/4\pi)]^{1/2}$. Crustal yielding is monitored dynamically using the von Mises criterion with threshold $\sigma_{\rm yield}=\mu_{\rm eff}\varepsilon_{\max}$ ($\varepsilon_{\max}=0.1$); failed cells permanently drop their effective shear modulus to $\mu_{\rm eff}=0$, dissipating elastic strain while conserving hydrodynamic inertia.
citation_leads: Magnetoelastic avalanches in magnetar crusts with plastic islands: “As crustal elements are displaced, shear stresses are tracked as a function of time to allow cells to dynamically switch from elastic to inelastic states.”
2 Mathematical model: “The aim of this work is to investigate how oscillations propagate in a magnetar crust that has regions that can dynamically switch from an elastic to an inelastic state.”
4.1 Time stepping and failure updating: “To choose a suitable timestep, we evaluate the largest local magnetoelastic wave speed on the grid,”
5.1 Failure progression: “The first involves a prompt avalanche: within $\approx 8$ ms over half the total failure count by simulation end has occurred”
5.1.2 Creeping failures: “Delayed failure and further drifting can arise from constructive interference between long-lived modes.”

6 Results: Localised quakes: “In this case, the elastic energy stored in the island is $E_{\rm el}=1.41\times 10^{43}$ erg and, with $\eta=0.05$, the initial pulse therefore contains an energy content of $E_{\rm kin,0}=7.07\times 10^{41}$ erg”
7 Discussion: “Allowing magnetic coupling to the core would change the boundary physics rather than merely add another damping coefficient.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed the first 2D time-domain relativistic solver coupling crustal magnetoelastic waves to dynamic von Mises yielding, establishing the physical mechanism of prompt avalanching and interference-induced creeping failure in magnetar bursts.

analysis.reason: This work introduces the FINEST finite-temperature equation of state (EOS) informed by ab initio chiral effective field theory and systematically quantifies how nuclear effective mass parameterizations affect core-collapse supernova (CCSN) central engine dynamics, neutrino heating, and fallback black hole formation.
analysis.result: Cold nuclear matter parameters introduce up to $\sim 150\text{ ms}$ delay in shock revival for high-compactness progenitors ($s24$, $\xi_{2.5}=0.44$), while very soft high-density matter ($P_{\rm SNM}=400\text{ MeV fm}^{-3}$) triggers black hole collapse within $500\text{ ms}$. Crucially, the thermal pressure is controlled by the nucleon effective mass $m^*$ via the thermal index $\Gamma_{\rm th} = 1 + P_{\rm th}/\epsilon_{\rm th} \approx \frac{5}{3} - \frac{n}{m^*}\frac{\partial m^*}{\partial n}$. A non-monotonic $m^*(n)$ functional ($m^*_{\rm HWS}$) reduces thermal pressure at densities exceeding saturation density $n_0$, accelerating protoneutron star (PNS) mantle contraction, which pushes neutrinospheres into hotter layers to enhance neutrino luminosity and successfully trigger delayed explosions, whereas standard monotonically decreasing Skyrme forms ($m^*_{\rm skyrme}$) fail to revive the shock and collapse into a black hole at $t_{\rm pb} \approx 1.65\text{ s}$.
analysis.reading_entry: IV Impact of the Effective Mass Parametrization
analysis.problem: Uncertainties in finite-temperature nuclear EOS tables—specifically the parameterizations of the in-medium nucleon effective mass $m^*(n)$ and high-density thermal pressure—remain poorly constrained by cold neutron star observations, leaving their direct impact on CCSN shock revival, neutrino-driven convection, and black hole formation ambiguous.
analysis.method: Constructed finite-temperature, composition-dependent EOS tables using the HWS energy-density functional with baryonic kinetic energy $\epsilon_{\rm kin}(n,y,T) = \frac{1}{n}\left(\frac{\hbar^2\tau_n}{2m_n^*} + \frac{\hbar^2\tau_p}{2m_p^*}\right)$ and a single-nucleus approximation transitioning smoothly into nuclear statistical equilibrium (NSE with 3335 nuclides). Performed spherically symmetric radiation-hydrodynamic CCSN simulations using FLASH with M1 two-moment three-flavor neutrino transport and STIR turbulence-assisted convection (mixing-length parameter $\alpha_\Lambda = 1.25$) on $s20$ and $s24$ progenitor models.
assumptions: Potential energy is independent of temperature: $\epsilon_B(n,y,T) = \epsilon_{\rm kin}(n,y,T) + \epsilon_{\rm pot}(n,y)$

analysis.reason: This study provides a systematic comparison of explodability, remnant masses, and detailed nucleosynthetic yields between single-star and binary-stripped core-collapse supernova progenitors, directly constraining central engine energetics and ejecta composition.
analysis.result: Progenitors with $M_{\rm ZAMS} \le 22\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ explode reliably across both populations, yielding explosion energies $E_{\rm exp} \sim 0.4\text{--}1.3\times 10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ ($0.4\text{--}1.3\text{ B}$), baryonic remnant masses $M_{\rm rem} \sim 1.4\text{--}2.0\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, and explosion timescales $t_{\rm exp} \sim 0.30\text{--}0.65\text{ s}$. The Salpeter IMF-weighted Fe yield for binary-stripped models is $0.0589\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ (consistent with empirical observations of $0.058 \pm 0.007\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$), while single-star progenitors yield $0.0747\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$. Binary stripping enhances K yields by $\sim 3.4$ times ($\sim 0.63\text{ dex}$) and systematically improves agreement with galactic [S/Mg], [K/Mg], and [Ca/Mg] trends.
analysis.reading_entry: 4.1 Two Representative Models: Ms18 and Mb18
analysis.problem: How binary interaction and envelope stripping modify the core compactness and pre-collapse progenitor structure of massive stars, and how these structural differences alter CCSN explodability, remnant properties, and nucleosynthetic yields across $M_{\rm ZAMS} = 11\text{--}45\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$.
analysis.method: One-dimensional general-relativistic hydrodynamic simulations using the Agile-PUSH framework to trigger shock revival via extra heating $Q_{\rm push}^+(t, r)$ parameterized by the bounce compactness $\xi_{2.0} = 2.0 / [R(M=2.0\,{\rm M}_\odot)/1000\,{\rm km}]$ via $k_{\rm push} = a\xi_{2.0}^2 + b\xi_{2.0} + c$, coupled with large nuclear network post-processing (CFNET, 2902 isotopes) following thermodynamic trajectories with peak temperatures $T_{\rm peak} > 1.75\,{\rm GK}$.
assumptions: Spherically symmetric 1D collapse and explosion can approximate the complex 3D neutrino-driven mechanism via a calibrated compactness-dependent push parameter $k_{\rm push}(\xi_{2.0})$.
limits: Simulations assume non-rotating solar-metallicity progenitors and parametric neutrino heating, causing explodability at $M_{\rm ZAMS} > 22\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ to depend sensitively on the exact phenomenological $k_{\rm push}$ calibration.

analysis.reason: This laboratory astrophysics study clarifies the structure and dynamics of the contact interface in laser-driven magnetized collisionless shocks, offering insights into shock formation and particle reflection relevant to supernova remnants and circumstellar interactions.
analysis.result: Using optical self-emission and collective Thomson scattering (CTS), the authors identify a rippling interface between the expanding laser-ablated Al piston and uniform N ambient plasma. Upstream parameters with $|B_{y0}| = 4\ \mathrm{T}$ yield an Alfvén speed $v_{\rm A} = |B_{y0}|/\sqrt{4\pi m_{\rm N}n_{\rm N}} \approx 92\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, which together with expansion velocity $V_{X^{\prime}} \approx 500\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ confirms a supercritical shock regime. CTS diagnoses electron density $n_e = (1.97\pm 0.26) \times 10^{18}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, $Z_{\rm Al} \approx 11$, and temperatures $T_e = 377\pm 19\ \mathrm{eV}$ and $T_i = 882\pm 16\ \mathrm{eV}$, confirming that the bright emission layer is dominated by piston Al plasma rather than compressed ambient plasma.
analysis.problem: In laboratory experiments of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, spatial inhomogeneity and boundary ambiguities make it difficult to determine whether detected reflected ions originate from the shock transition potential or the expanding piston-ambient plasma contact interface.
analysis.method: The authors perform laser-driven plasma interaction experiments on the Gekko-XII facility under a uniform $1.0\ \mathrm{Torr}$ nitrogen background and external magnetic fields ($B_{y0} = \pm 4\ \mathrm{T}$), combined with 2D single-fluid ideal-MHD simulations using Athena++ modeling synthetic bremsstrahlung intensity $I_s \propto n_e n_s Z_s^2 T_s^{-1/2} e^{-h\nu / k_{\rm B} T_s} \propto \sqrt{\rho_s^5 / P_s}\, (Z_s^3 / A_s^{5/2}) \exp[-h\nu\rho_s / (P_s A_s)]$.
limits: MHD simulations cannot capture the kinetic shock transition layer where the ion gyro-radius $r_{g,{\rm Al}} \approx 0.13\ \mathrm{cm}$ and ion inertial length $c/\omega_{pi} \sim 0.1\ \mathrm{cm}$ govern collisionless ion reflection.
citation_leads: I INTRODUCTION: “In quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, where the external upstream magnetic field is nearly perpendicular to the shock normal, it is well known that incoming ions are reflected by the shock potential”

III Analysis of Experimental Data: “Since the Alfvén speed of upstream plasma with $|B_{y0}|=4~\mathrm{T}$ is estimated as
$v_{\rm A}=|B_{y0}|/\sqrt{4\pi m_{\rm N}n_{\rm N}}\approx 92$ km s-1, where $m_{\rm N}$ is the mass of N ion,”
IV.2 Simulation setup: “The calculation is based on single-fluid MHD; the Al and N plasmas are not treated as separate fluids but are represented by different initial and boundary conditions.”

IV.3 Simulation Results: “Furthermore, assuming a finite-width velocity shear layer, we estimate the growth time of the KH instability for a wavelength of $\sim 0.15$ cm to be $\sim 100$ ns, which is significantly longer than the timescale of the system.”

V.1 Origin of density asymmetry in the Al plasma: “The resulting force drift of the electrons (i.e., $\vec{F}\times\vec{B}$ drift) is toward $+Z^{\prime}$ for $B_{y0}>0$ and toward $-Z^{\prime}$ for $B_{y0}<0$.”

V.2 Ion dynamics around the interface: “These parameters give $\lambda_{\rm ii}=1.3$ cm. Assuming $B_{\rm N}=10$ T, the Al-ion gyro-radius is $r_{\rm g,Al}=0.13$ cm, yielding $\lambda_{\rm ii}/r_{\rm g,Al}=10.2$.”
analysis.research_progress: The work demonstrates that the observed interface ripples do not originate from Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (whose growth timescale $\sim 100\ \mathrm{ns}$ at $\sim 0.15\ \mathrm{cm}$ wavelength exceeds the experiment duration) but arise from vortex motions at the rounded jet leading edge, while the field-dependent asymmetric expansion is driven by electron $\vec{F}\times\vec{B}$ drift.

analysis.reason: This paper presents critical deep HST and Gemini-N follow-up of the peculiar fast X-ray transient EP241021a, uncovering a sharp synchronous optical/X-ray drop at $\sim 47\ \mathrm{d}$ and an off-nuclear location ($0.95 \pm 0.13\ \mathrm{kpc}$) in a dwarf starburst galaxy, which directly constrains relativistic jet shut-off and long-duration non-SMBH tidal disruption engines.
analysis.result: EP241021a ($z = 0.748$, $D_L = 4.620\ \mathrm{Gpc}$, $E_{\mathrm{iso}} \lesssim 2 \times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$) occurred at a projected offset of $129 \pm 18\ \mathrm{mas}$ ($0.95 \pm 0.13\ \mathrm{kpc}$) from the nucleus of an edge-on dwarf starburst galaxy ($M_\star = (2.7 \pm 1.2) \times 10^8\ M_\odot$, $\mathrm{SFR} = 4.5 \pm 2.4\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, effective radius $R_e = 0.23'' \approx 1.7\ \mathrm{kpc}$). The host-subtracted optical transient underwent a rapid break/drop at observer-frame $t_{\mathrm{brk}} = 47.0^{+5.4}_{-3.7}\ \mathrm{d}$ (rest-frame $26.9^{+3.1}_{-2.1}\ \mathrm{d}$) at $\log(L_{\mathrm{brk}} / [\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}]) = 42.92 \pm 0.08$, synchronized with the X-ray light-curve steep decline. The month-long accretion timescale and off-nuclear site exclude both standard core-collapse supernova engines and supermassive black holes, favoring an intermediate-mass black hole ($M_{\mathrm{BH}} \lesssim 10^4\ M_\odot$) or a stellar-mass compact object micro-TDE undergoing repeating partial disruptions.
analysis.problem: Accounting for the multi-epoch optical rebrightenings (at $\sim 7.5\ \mathrm{d}$ with amplitude $\sim 2\ \mathrm{mag}$ and at $\sim 20\ \mathrm{d}$), the $\sim 1$-month flat X-ray plateau, and the subsequent coordinated steep drop at $40\!-\!50\ \mathrm{d}$, which break standard single-jet core-collapse supernova and compact binary merger models whose central engines shut down on timescales $\lesssim 10^3 - 10^4\ \mathrm{s}$.
analysis.method: Multi-band high-resolution imaging using HST/WFC3 (F606W, F814W, F110W, F160W) and Gemini-N/GMOS ($r, z$) combined with Gaia DR3 absolute astrometric calibration (galaxy centroid uncertainty $\sim 17\ \mathrm{mas}$) to measure the offset relative to VLBA coordinates; host-galaxy SED modeling via CIGALE to constrain $M_\star$, $\mathrm{SFR}$, age, and extinction; and host-subtracted light curve modeling parameterizing the post-break drop as jet cessation driven by cessation of accretion.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion in dense neutron star cores using multimessenger constraints (maximum mass $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$, GW170817 tidal deformability, and NICER mass-radius measurements). analysis.result: In-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion softens the nuclear EOS by reducing neutron fraction $Y_n$ and increasing dark fermion abundance $Y_\chi = n_\chi / n_B$. Weakly repulsive regimes ($G_\chi = 1$--$11~\mathrm{fm}^2$, $m_\chi = 939$--$1300~\mathrm{MeV}$) fail to support $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$ and are ruled out across the nuclear EOS ensemble. In the Illinois-Maryland analysis, the active conservative boundary is driven by $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$, while strict X-PSI/Amsterdam tests yield no common parameter point satisfying all 13 baseline EOSs, with the maximum compatibility ($N_{\rm cons} = 11$) confined to $m_\chi = 939$--$950~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $G_\chi = 19$--$21~\mathrm{fm}^2$.

analysis.problem: Whether in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion ($n \to \chi$), occurring when the neutron chemical potential exceeds the dark fermion mass ($\mu_n \ge m_\chi$), can survive multi-messenger astrophysical constraints from maximum neutron star masses ($M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$), GW170817 tidal deformabilities ($70 \le \Lambda_{1.4} \le 580$), and NICER mass-radius determinations across diverse nuclear EOSs.
analysis.method: A non-linear $\sigma$--$\omega$--$\rho$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) model is employed across an ensemble of 21 unified nucleonic EOSs. In dense matter, chemical equilibrium $\mu_\chi = \mu_n$ is solved self-consistently with $\beta$-equilibrium and charge neutrality, where the dark sector includes vector-meson-mediated repulsive self-interactions giving $\mu_\chi = \sqrt{k_{F,\chi}^2 + m_\chi^2} + G_\chi n_\chi$ with effective coupling $G_\chi \equiv (g_V / m_V)^2$ and energy density contribution $\varepsilon_{\chi\text{-int}} = \frac{1}{2} G_\chi n_\chi^2$.

analysis.reason: This work develops an analytical modeling framework for the gamma-ray morphology of TeV halos around moving pulsars, directly relevant to high-energy observations of compact objects and leptonic cosmic-ray transport.
analysis.result: The authors derive a closed-form analytical approximation for the projected line-of-sight (LOS) electron surface density $\Sigma(\rho,\phi,E) = \mathcal{S}(E)\mathcal{T}(\rho,\phi,E)$ around a moving pulsar. In the far-field limit $\rho, v\tau, r_d \ll d$, the 3D diffusion-loss convolution reduces to a single integral over injection history, and upon spatial integration $\int_0^{2\pi}d\phi\int_0^\infty \rho d\rho\,\Sigma$, the dependence on diffusion coefficient $D(E)$ and pulsar velocity $v$ strictly cancels, yielding an equilibrium lepton spectrum $N_{\rm eq}(E) \simeq q(E)\tau_{\max}(E)$.
analysis.problem: Pulsar proper motion ($v_{\rm psr} \sim 100\text{--}500\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) displaces the injection center over the cooling time $\tau_{\rm loss}(E)$, creating asymmetric, elongated TeV halo morphologies along the trajectory. Existing approaches require computationally prohibitive multi-dimensional numerical convolutions over LOS and injection history, hindering fast parameter inference and morphological fits to observational data from HAWC and LHAASO.
analysis.method: The framework models uniform pulsar motion $\mathbf{x}_{s}(t) = \mathbf{x}_{\rm age} + \mathbf{v}(t - t_{\rm age})$ with isotropic diffusion coefficient $D(E)$ and continuous injection $q(E, t)$. By completing the square along the LOS coordinate $\mathbf{x}_{\rm los} = \mathbf{x}_{\rm obs} + s\mathbf{n}$, the exact LOS integral is expressed in terms of the complementary error function $\mathrm{erfc}(a_n/r_d)$. In the far-field approximation, the spatial separation simplifies to $a^2 - a_n^2 \simeq \rho^2 + (v\tau)^2 + 2\rho v\tau\cos\phi$, and introducing the dimensionless parameters $\chi = \tau/\tau_D$, $\eta = \tau_v/\tau_D = 4D(E)/(\rho v)$ allows closed-form integration using modified Bessel functions $K_0$ and error functions $\mathrm{erf}$.

analysis.problem: Investigating the physical origin of the rare double X-ray plateau, the abrupt decay accompanied by strong spectral softening, and the delayed, rapidly rising radio afterglow in the extragalactic fast X-ray transient EP251129a.
analysis.method: Multi-wavelength data analysis combining EP-FXT, Swift-XRT, Chandra, optical facilities, and radio telescopes (VLA, e-MERLIN). Theoretical modeling incorporates millisecond magnetar spin-down dominated by gravitational wave radiation ($L_{\mathrm{EM}}(t) \simeq L_{\mathrm{em},0}(1+t/\tau_{c,\mathrm{gw}})^{-1}$), collapse to a black hole, dynamic forward shock in a wind medium ($\rho = A R^{-2}$) with a two-component off-axis jet (core angle $\theta_{\rm c}$, wing angle $\theta_{\rm j}$), and Blandford-Znajek fallback accretion energy injection ($L_{\rm BZ} \propto \dot{M}$).
assumptions: The early internal plateau is powered by the spin-down dissipation of a supramassive millisecond magnetar initially dominated by gravitational wave emission.

Late-time afterglow emission originates from an off-axis two-component jet propagating into a stellar wind medium ($\rho = A R^{-2}$) with fallback accretion energy injection via the Blandford-Znajek mechanism.
limits: Late-time X-ray photon statistics are limited, requiring tied photon indices across adjacent epochs.
A pure black hole fallback model for the early internal plateau is disfavored due to strong off-axis Doppler de-beaming ($F_{\nu,\rm off} \approx a^{3+\beta_X} F_{\nu,\rm on}$) with $a \sim 10^{-3}$.

analysis.result: When the threshold condition $\mu_n + \mu_e > M_{\Delta^-}^* + U_{\Delta^-}$ is met, the three-body absorption reaction $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$ dominates the opacity, suppressing the antineutrino Rosseland mean free path $\lambda_R$ from $3\text{--}300\text{ m}$ down to $0.5\text{--}16\text{ cm}$ (a reduction factor of $83$ to $4.5\times 10^4$) at densities of $2\text{--}4n_0$. Consequently, the antineutrino share of the lepton-number diffusion coefficient $D_2$ drops from up to $69\%$ to below $7\%$, reducing total lepton diffusion by up to a factor of 3 at $Y_L=0.1$, while total energy diffusion $D_4$ changes by $<2\%$.

analysis.result: Linear interpolation of non-linear models introduces a single-parameter error $e(\theta) = m(\theta) - \tilde{m}(\theta) = -\frac{1}{2} m''(\xi)(\theta - \theta_i)(\theta_{i+1} - \theta)$, which distorts the log-likelihood by adding a quadratic penalty $-\frac{1}{2} \sum_k \frac{e_k^2(\theta)}{\sigma_k^2}$ and a residual cross-term $-\sum_k \frac{e_k(\theta)[d_k - m_k(\theta)]}{\sigma_k^2}$. Its first derivative $\frac{d \ln \tilde{\mathcal{L}}}{d \theta} = \frac{d \ln \mathcal{L}}{d \theta} - \sum_k \frac{e_k e'_k - e_k m'_k + e'_k (d_k - m_k)}{\sigma_k^2}$ introduces discontinuous jumps at grid points via $e'_k(d_k - m_k)$, generating artificial modes. In real NuSTAR fits of MAXI J1820+070, table models induced artificial multimodality (e.g., spin $a$, photon index $\Gamma = 1.6$), causing affine-invariant MCMC acceptance rates to drop to $\approx 5\%$ and autocorrelation times to blow up to $\tau \approx 4000\text{--}16000$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the discovery and characterization of DGL-3, an ultra-short-period ($P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$) binary in the SMC hosting an intermediate-mass stripped star and an unseen compact companion ($M_2 \approx 1.58\,M_\odot$), providing direct observational evidence of an immediate progenitor to a merging double neutron star system.
analysis.result: The spectroscopic and photometric analysis shows the binary has orbital period $P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$, semi-amplitude $K = 151.4 \pm 2.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, and circular orbit ($e < 0.045$ at 95% credible limit). The mass function $f(m) = \frac{P K^3}{2\pi G} = 0.062 \pm 0.003\,M_\odot$ yields a minimum companion mass $M_{2,\min} = 1.38 \pm 0.25\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$), with ellipsoidal light-curve modeling yielding a posterior peak of $M_2 = 1.58\,M_\odot$ (68% HDI: $[1.40 - 2.41]\,M_\odot$), identifying the companion as a compact object (most likely a neutron star). analysis.reason: The paper presents full nonlinear hydrodynamical simulations and an analytical mode-coupling framework for binary neutron star late inspirals, quantifying nonlinear tidal frequency shifts and gravitational-wave phase shifts relevant to compact object mergers.
analysis.result: In the late inspiral stage ($D = 2.5 R_*$), nonlinear tidal interactions reduce the neutron star quadrupole fundamental mode ($f$-mode) frequency by $\sim 10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and impart an extra gravitational-wave phase shift of $\Delta \Phi_X \sim \mathcal{O}(1)\ \mathrm{rad}$ beyond the linear tidal response up to $f_{\rm GW} = 1100\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The second-order perturbative frequency shift scales as $\Delta f^{(2)} \propto q^2$ (where $q = M_c / M_*$), and the radial mode frequency drops by $8.8\%$ to $f_r = 0.3173$ due to nonlinear $c_{20}$–$c_r$ coupling.
analysis.reading_entry: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
analysis.problem: Linear tidal theory assumes that external tidal driving forces a response without shifting stellar eigenfrequencies, breaking down during late binary inspirals where strong nonlinear mode couplings alter the restoring forces and induce unmodeled phase errors in gravitational-wave templates.
analysis.method: Solves the complete 3D Newtonian nonlinear Euler-Poisson equations for non-rotating $\Gamma=2$ polytropes using Athena++ under a time-varying quadrupolar tidal potential $U_{\rm tide}(\bm{x}, t)$, coupled with an analytical multi-mode coupling model incorporating $l=0$ radial and $l=2, 4$ $f$-modes via three-mode and four-mode coupling coefficients ($\kappa_{abc}$, $\zeta_{abcd}$), and incorporates Burke-Thorne radiation reaction terms $a_i^{\rm BT}$ to trace self-consistent orbital and phase evolution.
assumptions: Slowly evolving, nearly circular orbit approximation for radiation reaction formulations
limits: Second-order perturbative truncation of mode frequency shift fails at late inspiral separations ($D \lesssim 2.5 R_*$)

analysis.reason: This work presents an observational indication of electron antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB) with Super-Kamiokande, yielding a 2.6 sigma tension with the null hypothesis and critical constraints on core-collapse supernova physics.
analysis.reading_entry: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
analysis.problem: Detecting electron antineutrinos from the cumulative past core-collapse supernovae (DSNB) against overwhelming backgrounds from atmospheric neutrino neutral-current and charged-current interactions as well as cosmic-ray muon spallation products.
analysis.method: Analysis of 5003.0 days of Super-Kamiokande data (pure water and Gd-loaded SK-VI to SK-VIII phases) detecting inverse beta decay $\bar{\nu}_{e} + p \to e^{+} + n$ via an unbinned extended maximum likelihood fit across 6 subregions defined by Cherenkov angle $\theta_{\mathrm{C}}$ and tagged neutron multiplicity $N_{\rm n}$, incorporating machine learning for NC background rejection and an optimized threshold of $E_{\rm rec} = 11.5\text{ MeV}$ for $N_{\rm n} = 1$.
assumptions: DSNB signal follows core-collapse supernova neutrino emission models (such as Horiuchi+09 6 MeV, Kresse+21, or Ashida+23).
limits: Signal significance stands at $2.6\sigma$, which represents an observational indication rather than a definitive $5\sigma$ discovery.
citation_leads: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background: “Using a representative DSNB model, the best-fit flux was determined to be $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ for $E_{\nu}>13.3$ MeV, corresponding to a $2.6\sigma$ tension with a null hypothesis”

Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background: “Systematic uncertainties for the atmospheric $\nu$ backgrounds arise from the interaction rate (flux times cross section) and the final-state kinematics ($\gamma$ ray and neutron multiplicities).”
References: “The fraction of the expected signal in the higher-purity $N_{\rm n}=1$ subregion increases from 42% with a common threshold of $E_{\rm rec}=15.5$ MeV to 60% with the new thresholds.”
analysis.research_progress: Lowers the reconstructed energy threshold for $N_{\rm n}=1$ to $E_{\rm rec} = 11.5\text{ MeV}$ (corresponding to $E_{\nu} > 13.3\text{ MeV}$) using Gd neutron tagging, reducing NCQE contamination to $5\%$ and achieving the first $2.6\sigma$ measurement of the DSNB $\bar{\nu}_e$ flux.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Energy spectra of the data and expected backgrounds in the $N_{\text{n}}=1$ signal region. The grey hatch represents the total uncertainty on the expected backgrounds. The nominal Horiuchi+09 DSNB model prediction [ 60 ] is overlaid for reference.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first ultra-long GRMHD simulation of a black hole accretion torus up to $t_{\rm max} = 10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$ and benchmarks it against relativistic thin disk theory, providing valuable insights into the late-time evolution of accretion engines, outflows, and TDE plateau phases.
analysis.result: The long-term evolution of the bound accretion disk and mass accretion rate follows power-law decay behaviors: $\dot{M}(t) \propto t^{-n}$ with $n=(4-2\mu)/(3-2\mu)$, outer disk radius $r_{\rm out} \sim \sigma_{\rm eff}(t) \sim t^{2/(3-2\mu)} \sim t^{2n-2}$, and peak line mass $M'_{\rm max} \sim t^{1-n}$. For a scale-independent turbulent stress $W^r_\phi \approx w \approx 0.05$ ($\mu = 0, n = 4/3$), General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory (GRTDT) reproduces disk spreading within a factor of $\sim 2$, though it over-predicts the horizon accretion rate by a factor of $\sim 2$ at $t \gtrsim 2\times 10^4\,t_{\rm g}$ because unbound disk winds carry away $\sim 50\%\text{--}80\%$ of the lost mass.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.2 General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory
analysis.problem: Whether simplified general relativistic thin disk theory (GRTDT) remains applicable to thick ($H/r \sim 1$), magnetically arrested (MAD) accretion flows over secular viscous timescales up to $10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$, and how non-local magnetic torques, disk winds, and turbulent stress affect long-term disk spreading.
analysis.method: Ideal GRMHD simulations on a Schwarzschild metric performed with AthenaK using Cartesian Kerr-Schild coordinates, adaptive mesh refinement, and a novel cyclic zoom algorithm to reach $t_{\rm max} = 10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$. These numerical results are compared against analytical Green's function solutions of height-integrated, vertically averaged GRTDT governing equations: $\partial\Sigma/\partial t = (r\overline{U}^t)^{-1}\partial_r [(\overline{U}_\phi')^{-1}\partial_r (r\Sigma W^r_\phi)]$ with turbulent stress parameterization $W^r_\phi = w(r/r_0)^\mu(\rho/\rho_0)^\eta$.
limits: GRTDT neglects disk winds/mass loss, which carry away the majority of lost bound mass at late times.
citation_leads: The long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus: a comparison between GRMHD simulations and relativistic thin disk theory: “In this paper we analyse the long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus using novel GRMHD simulations”
III.1 The fundamental equations of ideal GRMHD: “In GRMHD one solves the coupled equations of mass conservation, energy-momentum conservation, and the Maxwell equations”
V.1 A comparison of the summary statistics: “GRTDT over-predicts the horizon accretion rate by a factor $\sim 2$ at $t\gtrsim 2\times 10^{4}\,t_{\mathrm{g}}$”
VI.3 Successes of analytical theories: “Global conservation laws strongly constrain the bulk of the disk evolution: once the accretion rate is known to decay”
IV.3 Properties of GRTDT solutions: “the equivalent width of the mass distribution inherits the same time dependence as the outer disk radius”
VI.2 Could the evolution have been otherwise?: “by late times only $\sim 20\%$ of the mass lost by the bound gas is accreted, the remainder being transferred”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that global mass and angular momentum conservation constrain the bulk evolution of thick MAD accretion disks to behave quasi-diffusively, proving that $\sigma_{\rm eff} \propto r_{\rm out} \propto t^{2n-2}$ and that the fractional variability spectrum displays a broken red noise power law with break frequency $f_b \approx 10^{-3}\,t_{\rm g}^{-1}$, steepening from $P(f) \propto f^{-0.45}$ to $P(f) \propto f^{-2.06}$.

figures.caption: Figure 6: The four accretion flow summary statistics introduced in section II, and a comparison between simulation data (black dots) and GRTDT (blue dot-dashed curves). This plot is for the traditional GRMHD run, which saves the mass accretion rate (upper left panel) at higher cadence than the three $M^{\prime}$ summary statistics, which require the full simulation data to compute (as opposed to the data local to the horizon). Both $\dot{M}$ and $M^{\prime}_{\rm max}$ are displayed in code units, while $r_{\rm max}$ and $\sigma_{\rm eff}$ are displayed in units of gravitational radii. The time axis on each plot is displayed in units of gravitational times. In the upper left panel the dotted curve shows the GRTDT horizon accretion rate with the same normalization as the mass distribution (i.e., with no free parameters), while the dot-dashed curve shows the same prediction renormalized by a factor $\sim 1/2$ to approximately match the simulation, to allow the time dependence to be compared. The difference between the two reflects the fraction of the bound mass loss which is transferred to the outflow rather than accreted (section VI.1.3, Figure 9 ). The effective width $\sigma_{\rm eff}$ is defined identically for both theories (half the distance between the two radii at which $M^{\prime}=M^{\prime}_{\rm max}/\sqrt{e}$); as neither mass distribution is Gaussian, this comparison is approximate.
figures.label: Fig. 6
figures.physical_core: 将 GRMHD 模拟的黑洞吸积率及束缚盘质量分布统计量，与广义相对论薄盘理论（GRTDT）作时间演化对比。图中比较了 $\dot{M}$、$M'_{\rm max}$、$r_{\rm max}$ 和 $\sigma_{\rm eff}$；GRTDT 在吸积率曲线上的归一化差异还体现了束缚物质损失中流入外流而非落入黑洞的部分。

figures.caption: Figure 7: A visual comparison of the evolution of $M^{\prime}$ for classical GRMHD (left panel) and the equivalent evolution for GRTDT (right panel). The color of each curve denotes the time of the snapshot, as shown by the color bar shared by both panels; the snapshots span more than two orders of magnitude in time, from $t_{1}\approx 5\times 10^{3}\,t_{\mathrm{g}}$ to $t_{2}\approx 10^{6}\,t_{\mathrm{g}}$. There is a striking similarity in the global evolution, with clear agreement on key evolutionary features between the two techniques.
figures.label: Fig. 7

analysis.reason: This paper presents the complete instrument architecture, flight performance, and calibration of PUEO, a premier balloon-borne experiment targeting ultrahigh-energy neutrinos ($E \gtrsim 1\text{ EeV}$) and cosmic rays via Askaryan radio impulses and EAS radio emission.
analysis.result: PUEO successfully operated during a 23-day Antarctic flight with an average livetime fraction of $\sim 55\%$ (limited by thermal constraints to keep RFSoC temperatures below $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$), collecting $114,046,211$ RF trigger events. Ground-testing confirmed a $50\%$ trigger efficiency threshold at $\mathrm{SNR} = 1.4$ (over twice as sensitive as ANITA-IV). The multi-antenna GNSS orientation achieved smoothed pitch and roll standard deviations of $0.015^\circ$ and $0.024^\circ$, and heading residuals of $0.070^\circ$ after applying a spin-dependent time-lag correction $\text{Heading} = \text{Heading} - \tau\cdot\omega$.
analysis.problem: Detecting extremely low flux ultrahigh-energy neutrinos ($E \gtrsim 1\text{ EeV}$) requires monitoring massive target volumes ($\sim 10^6\text{ km}^3$) of Antarctic ice while achieving trigger sensitivity near the thermal noise floor and discriminating genuine impulsively coherent Askaryan or air shower signals from anthropogenic RF interference and thermal fluctuations.
analysis.method: PUEO incorporates a 96-horn dual-polarization main antenna array ($300-1200\text{ MHz}$) coupled to a real-time digital interferometric phased-array trigger implemented on 26 Xilinx RFSoC ZU47DR modules sampling at $3\text{ GSa/s}$, synthesizing 48 simultaneous coherent beams. Signal classification on the science computer uses coherent summation and Hilbert envelope energy concentration ($<10\%$ envelope duration containing $30\%$ total power for high-priority signals) alongside calibration pulses from ground pulsers and twin HiCal-3 balloons.
limits: Instrument duty cycle was restricted to an overall average of $\sim 55\%$ to maintain RFSoC FPGA temperatures below the $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$ threshold.
citation_leads: 3.1.1 Objectives: “Increasing total exposure gives PUEO higher odds of observing neutrinos and, in the case of a non-detection, allows for more stringent limits to be set on the neutrino flux at ultrahigh energies.”
3.2 Top-Level Design: “All electronics systems are housed inside RF-sealed (in most cases, using gasketing) metal Faraday enclosures that utilize shielded cables for input, output, and power.”

3.4.2 AMPAs and Receivers: “The noise temperature of the chain has a max specification of $80$ K between $300$ and $700$ MHz in order to remain a subdominant contribution to the trigger thermal noise”

3.7.1 Hardware: “The DAQ is split into two main crates, one for each polarization (Hpol and Vpol), consisting of 12 SURFv6 modules. An additional two SURFv6 modules are present in the Hpol crate to digitize the LF instrument channels, for a total of 26”

3.10.3 Prioritizer Algorithms: “Signal-like: Events that reconstruct below horizontal and have coherently summed Hilbert Envelopes where most of the power is emitted in a short, configurable time period are promoted to high signal-like ranks.”

7.1 Flight Path and Livetime: “The duty cycle of the instrument was managed during the flight to keep the RFSoC temperatures below 80∘C, with the RFSoC clocks and processors turned off during the recovery portion of the cycle. This resulted in an overall average duty”

7.3 Navigation: “Since there is a clear linear structure to these modes, we have corrected for them with a spin-dependent correction of $\text{Heading}=\text{Heading}-\tau\cdot\omega$, where $\tau$ is the appropriate slope based on the mode.”
analysis.research_progress: Achieved a factor of $>2$ improvement in trigger SNR threshold ($\%50$ efficiency at $\mathrm{SNR} = 1.4$) relative to ANITA-IV through RFSoC-based real-time beamforming, combined with low-frequency ($50-500\text{ MHz}$) air shower instrumentation and sub-$0.1^\circ$ attitude reconstruction.

Neutrinos can be detected via the channel of tau-decay on the left or in-ice Askaryan emission on the right. An inset diagram of the payload as flown is shown on the top right.

analysis.reason: This paper formulates the nonlinear perturbation theory and induced scattering instability of strong superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves propagating through magnetized electron-positron pair plasmas, directly relevant to FRB propagation through magnetar winds.
analysis.result: The authors derive the perturbation dynamics and coupled dispersion relation for the induced scattering instability, $D_{\rm v}^{2}-f_{0}\Omega_{\rm B}^{2}\simeq\frac{2\eta^{3}}{\omega}k(\Omega+k)\left(\frac{1}{D_{+}}+\frac{1}{D_{-}}\right)$, where $D_{\rm v}\equiv\Omega+v_{x}k$, $D_{\pm}\equiv(\Omega\pm\omega)^{2}-k^{2}-\omega_{\rm p}^{2}$, and the scattering parameter is $\eta\equiv\omega({\cal A}\varepsilon_{\rm p}/2)^{2/3}$. In the strong-coupling limit ($\Omega_{\rm B}\ll\eta$), the maximum growth rate scales as $\Gamma_{\rm gr}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\eta$, while in the weak-coupling limit ($\Omega_{\rm B}\gg\eta$), the instability growth is modified by the magnetic restoring frequency $\Omega_{\rm B}\equiv\sqrt{1+\hat{a}^{2}/2}(\omega_{\rm B}/\gamma_{0})$.

opening_brief.intro: 本期首看《EP241021a as An Off-nuclear Month-duration Transient in a Dwarf Starburst Galaxy》等 38 篇核心进展。

must_read.label: EP241021a as An Off-nuclear Month-duration Transient in a Dwarf Starburst Galaxy
must_read.text: EP241021a ($z = 0.748$, $D_L = 4.620\ \mathrm{Gpc}$, $E_{\mathrm{iso}} \lesssim 2 \times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$) occurred at a projected offset of $129 \pm 18\ \mathrm{mas}$ ($0.95 \pm 0.13\ \mathrm{kpc}$) from the nucleus of an edge-on dwarf starburst galaxy ($M_\star = (2.7 \pm 1.2) \times 10^8\ M_\odot$, $\mathrm{SFR} = 4.5 \pm 2.4\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, effective radius $R_e = 0.23'' \approx 1.7\ \mathrm{kpc}$).

must_read.label: EP251129a: A Fast X-ray Transient with Two X-Ray Plateaus and Its Off-axis Afterglow
must_read.text: EP251129a at $z = 0.505$ exhibits an early internal X-ray plateau ($\alpha_{\mathrm{X},1}=0.93$) terminating at $t_{\mathrm{X},1} = 1.27 \times 10^4\,\mathrm{s}$ with a steep drop ($\alpha_{\mathrm{X},2} = 5.28$) and spectral softening ($\Gamma_{\mathrm{X}}$ softening from $\simeq 2.1$ to $\simeq 3.6$), followed by a second plateau ($\alpha_{\mathrm{X},3} = 0.42$) up to $\sim 42\,\mathrm{days}$ in rest frame.

must_read.label: An Intermediate Mass Stripped Star in a 4.2-hour Orbit around a Compact Object
must_read.text: The spectroscopic and photometric analysis shows the binary has orbital period $P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$, semi-amplitude $K = 151.4 \pm 2.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, and circular orbit ($e < 0.045$ at 95% credible limit).

must_read.label: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
must_read.text: Using a representative DSNB model (Horiuchi+09 with $T = 6\text{ MeV}$), the best-fit $\bar{\nu}_e$ flux is $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}\text{ cm}^{-2}\,\text{s}^{-1}$ for $E_{\nu} > 13.3\text{ MeV}$ (corresponding to an event rate of $4.8^{+2.2}_{-2.0}\text{ events}\,\text{yr}^{-1}$), rejecting the null hypothesis at $2.6\sigma$.

must_read.label: The design and flight of the Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations (PUEO)
must_read.text: PUEO successfully operated during a 23-day Antarctic flight with an average livetime fraction of $\sim 55\%$ (limited by thermal constraints to keep RFSoC temperatures below $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$), collecting $114,046,211$ RF trigger events.
